question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool indicate a probability of at least 60% for a 25-bps or greater rate cut at the January 2026 meeting between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18?

The decision was made in light of moderated economic activity, slowed job gains, and somewhat elevated inflation <https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm>. The CME FedWatch tool currently indicates a 93.2% probability of a 25-bps cut at the October meeting and a 92.7% probability of a further 25-bps cut at the December meeting <https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/fedwatch.html>. Sources: 
Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm 
CME Group: https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/fedwatch.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CME FedWatch tool indicates a probability of at least 60% for a 25-bps or greater rate cut at the January 2026 meeting between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18. The resolution source will be the CME FedWatch tool, available at https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/interest-rates/fedwatch.html. The start date for this question is 2025-09-18 and the end date is 2025-10-18.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it gauges market expectations for the January 2026 meeting, which can influence the actual decision made by the Federal Reserve. A high probability of a rate cut indicated by the CME FedWatch tool may suggest that the market expects the Fed to decrease interest rates, potentially by 50 bps or more, in January 2026.

evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'CME FedWatch January 2026 rate cut probability' (Sept 18-Oct 18, 2025) - to find direct references; 2) 'Federal Reserve interest rate cut January 2026 probability odds' - to find market pricing; 3) 'CME FedWatch January 2026 FOMC meeting rate cut probability 60%' - to find threshold crossing; 4) 'Federal Reserve January 2026 meeting rate cut futures market probability' - broader search; 5) 'Fed January 2026 FOMC rate cut expected probability Wall Street' - to find analyst commentary
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (A) Morningstar/MarketWatch (Sept 25, 2025): CME FedWatch shows 85.5% probability for a cut at the October 2026 meeting - this implies strong cutting expectations into 2026 but refers to Oct 2026, not Jan 2026. (D) USD/JPY Q4 Outlook (Oct 3, 2025): '100 basis points of Fed rate cuts by July 2026' - cumulative, not specific to January 2026. (E) Multiple articles mention December 2025 cut probabilities of 80-90%. None of these explicitly state CME FedWatch's probability for the January 2026 FOMC meeting specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found that explicitly states the CME FedWatch probability for the January 2026 FOMC meeting during the window Sep 18 - Oct 18, 2025. The closest evidence: [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20250925235/wall-street-is-starting-to-rethink-the-need-for-multiple-rate-cuts-into-2026) (Sept 25) states 85.5% probability for October 2026 cut. [Investing.com India](https://in.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-riskmanagement-cuts-still-in-play-despite-upward-us-gdp-revision--ms-5020791) (Sept 26) states '62% probability in December' referring to December 2025. None explicitly reports on CME FedWatch January 2026 probability.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp can be extracted for the specific condition (CME FedWatch ≥60% for January 2026 FOMC meeting) because no source explicitly reports this figure during the window.

evidence.step7_verification: Context strongly suggests January 2026 cut probability was likely above 60% during the window: (1) The September 25 Morningstar article shows 85.5% for October 2026 cuts - implying January 2026 would be at least as high; (2) Multiple analysts forecast multiple 2026 cuts; (3) The Fed's dot plot projected one cut in 2026 but markets were pricing far more. However, this is inferential - the question requires explicit CME FedWatch data for January 2026 specifically. I cannot verify this without direct evidence. Contextual evidence is insufficient per the strict resolution rules.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While contextual evidence strongly suggests that CME FedWatch was showing ≥60% probability for a January 2026 rate cut during the window (given 85.5% for October 2026 cuts was reported, and markets were pricing far more cuts than the Fed projected), no article explicitly reports the CME FedWatch probability specifically for the January 2026 FOMC meeting. question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) report a seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP of less than 2.0% for Q3 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The US economy has shown signs of slowing down, with a contraction in real GDP in the first quarter of 2025. However, the second quarter saw a growth rate of 3.3%, driven by a decrease in imports and an increase in consumer spending. The BEA's advance estimate for Q2 2025 exceeded expectations, with a 3.0% annualized increase. The current state of the economy is uncertain, with some economists predicting a recession and others expecting a shallow and brief downturn. According to the BEA, the real GDP growth rate for the first quarter of 2025 was revised to -0.2%, and the second quarter saw a growth rate of 3.3% https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) defines a recession as a 'significant decline in economic activity that is spread across the economy and that lasts more than a few months' https://www.nber.org/. Sources: 
Bureau of Economic Analysis, https://www.bea.gov/
National Bureau of Economic Research, https://www.nber.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the BEA reports a seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP of less than 2.0% for Q3 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, as reported on the BEA's website https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. The resolution source will be the official announcements from the BEA.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides an early indicator of the US economy's performance in Q3 2025. A growth rate of less than 2.0% could indicate a slowing down of the economy, which might increase the likelihood of a recession in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: BEA must publish seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in real GDP for Q3 2025 (July–September 2025) that is less than 2.0%, published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: Official BEA press release or data page showing Q3 2025 GDP figure during that window. Key constraint: Q3 2025 ends September 30, 2025 — the BEA advance estimate is always released ~4 weeks after quarter end, meaning no Q3 2025 GDP figure could be available before October 1.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BEA US GDP Q3 2025 third quarter advance estimate release' (to find when Q3 2025 GDP was scheduled); Query 2: 'Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP report September 2025' (to find any BEA GDP report in the window); Query 3: 'BEA Q3 2025 GDP advance estimate October 30 release date schedule' (to confirm scheduled date); Query 4: 'US real GDP third quarter 2025 report BEA release September October' (to look for any Q3 2025 GDP report in window).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) BEA released Q2 2025 GDP final (third) estimate of 3.8% on September 25, 2025 — REJECTED: this is Q2 2025 data, not Q3 2025. (2) BEA advance estimate for Q3 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025 — outside the window. No Q3 2025 GDP report was published between September 1 and October 1, 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires a BEA report of Q3 2025 GDP data between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Multiple sources confirm the advance estimate for Q3 2025 was scheduled for October 30, 2025 [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/map-shows-which-states-economies-are-growing-and-shrinking-this-year-10790529), [EconoTimes](https://econotimes.com/US-Government-Shutdown-Threatens-Release-of-Key-Economic-Data-1721918), [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/content/gdp-nowcasts-still-indicate-moderate-us-growth-for-q3?post=527628). No Q3 2025 GDP figure was published by the BEA within the required window. The criteria are definitively not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp exists for a Q3 2025 BEA GDP report within the window, because no such report was issued. The earliest possible release of Q3 2025 GDP data was October 30, 2025 (scheduled), which is outside the window.
evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. BEA's standard release schedule means Q3 2025 (July–September) GDP data cannot be reported until late October 2025 at the earliest. A government shutdown beginning October 1, 2025 further confirmed that no Q3 GDP data would emerge during the September 1–October 1 window. The only BEA GDP release in the window was the Q2 2025 final estimate (3.8%) on September 25, 2025, which is not Q3 2025 data.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The BEA did not and could not have reported Q3 2025 GDP between September 1 and October 1, 2025 — Q3 2025 had not yet ended by October 1, and the advance estimate was scheduled for October 30, 2025. The condition became definitively impossible given the BEA's standard release calendar, confirmed by the end of the resolution window on 2025-10-01.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?
description:

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Japan's January 2026 meeting.

If the short-term policy interest rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Bank of Japan (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Japan's statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question cannot be definitively resolved. description:

subquestions.question: Will the total number of ICE deportations from January 1, 2025, to February 26, 2026, exceed 550,000?
subquestions.background_information:
The Trump administration has set a goal of deporting 600,000 people in 2025, with 548,000 individuals already removed from the U.S. by October 19, 2025, according to Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/trump-administration-aiming-600000-deportations-2025-1774447). ICE data shows a steady rise in immigrants self-deporting, with voluntary departures rising from 592 in February to 4,241 by July 2025, as reported by Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/ice-data-shows-steady-rise-immigrants-self-deporting-1774448). The current pace of deportations is on track to reach 600,000 by year-end, according to The Bellingham Herald (https://www.bellinghamherald.com/news/nation-world/national/article267341107.html). Sources: 
Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/
The Bellingham Herald: https://www.bellinghamherald.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the total number of ICE deportations from January 1, 2025, to February 26, 2026, exceeds 550,000, according to data from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) website (https://www.ice.gov/) or other credible sources such as Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/) or The Bellingham Herald (https://www.bellinghamherald.com/). The resolution window is from 2026-01-29 to 2026-02-26.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides an indicator of the Trump administration's progress towards its deportation goal. If the total number of ICE deportations exceeds 550,000 by February 26, 2026, it suggests that the administration is on track to meet its goal of 600,000 deportations in 2025, which would increase the likelihood of reaching the ultimate question's threshold of 750,000 deportations.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Total ICE deportations from Jan 1, 2025 to Feb 26, 2026 must exceed 550,000. Observable evidence: Official ICE or credible news data showing cumulative count >550,000. Key entities: ICE, DHS. Threshold: 550,000. Timing: Jan 1, 2025–Feb 26, 2026, resolution window Jan 29–Feb 26, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'ICE deportations total number 2025 statistics' (Jan–Feb 2026); 2) 'ICE removals deportations cumulative total Trump administration 2025' (Jun 2025–Feb 2026); 3) 'ICE deportations 550000 total 2025 2026'; 4) 'Trump deportation total count January 2025 February 2026 cumulative'; 5) 'DHS ICE deportation data 713000 675000 formal removals 2025'; 6) 'Seattle Times 540000 deportations Trump first year analysis'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate data points: (A) DHS claimed 622,000 deportations in 2025 [Center Square, Dec 26 2025], and 675,000–713,000 by Feb 2026 [DHS/Newsweek Feb 25 2026]; (B) Seattle Times (Jan 28, 2026) estimated ~540,000 combined deportations for Jan 20, 2025–Jan 20, 2026; (C) Deportation Data Project: ~350,000 deported Jan 20, 2025–early Feb 2026, excluding border encounters; (D) Irish Times (Feb 17, 2026): ~290,000 deported; (E) Straits Times State of Union summary (Feb 25, 2026): 540,000 in past year. Rejected: DW estimate of ~300,000 (Trump 2nd term only, unclear methodology). All figures face definitional and scope issues.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The question requires ICE-specific deportations starting Jan 1, 2025 (not Jan 20 inauguration). Critical problems: (1) DHS figures of 622,000–713,000 are disputed and include all agencies (ICE, CBP, others), not ICE alone — [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/3-million-undocumented-immigrants-have-left-us-trump-administration-11581214) explicitly notes 'Newsweek could not independently verify the figures, and DHS has removed deportation data from its public website.' (2) Independent estimates (Deportation Data Project, cited by Newsweek) show only ~350,000 ICE deportations Jan 20–Feb 2026, excluding border encounters, well below 550,000. (3) [Seattle Times](https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/how-many-people-has-trump-deported-so-far/) analysis gives 540,000 for Jan 20–Jan 20, 2026, which includes all deportation types including border removals, starting 20 days later than required. (4) The [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trumps-state-of-the-union-by-the-numbers) State of the Union summary states '~540,000 in the past year,' noting it 'fell short of the 1 million goal.' (5) DHS specifically removed deportation data from its website, making official verification impossible. Figures vary from ~290,000 to 713,000+ depending on definitions and sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No single exact timestamp can be extracted because: (a) the data is cumulative with various cutoff dates; (b) no single authoritative source with a precise cumulative total as of Feb 26, 2026 was identified; (c) DHS data removed from website; (d) conflicting numbers prevent pinpointing when/if the threshold was crossed.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — cannot establish even whether the threshold was met, much less the first occurrence date.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: DHS claims 713,000 formal deportations by Feb 25, 2026 (exceeds threshold if trusted) vs. Deportation Data Project's 350,000 (well below threshold). The Seattle Times independently computed ~540,000 for Jan 20–Jan 20, 2026 — this is close to the 550,000 threshold but: (a) covers a slightly different time window (starting Jan 20 not Jan 1); (b) includes CBP border removals not just ICE; (c) ends Jan 20, not Feb 26 — additional deportations in the 37 days through Feb 26 could push it over 550,000. However, the question specifically asks about 'ICE deportations,' and independent ICE-only data (Deportation Data Project) shows only ~350,000. DHS has removed its data and its figures are disputed as inflated. The evidence is deeply conflicting and cannot be resolved without authoritative, verified data.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is not determinable with confidence. The DHS government figures (622,000–713,000) would suggest Yes, but: they are disputed by independent researchers, include all agencies not just ICE, DHS removed the data from its website, and Newsweek explicitly could not verify them. Independent data (Deportation Data Project, ICE-specific) shows ~290,000–350,000, well below 550,000. The Seattle Times analysis of ~540,000 (Jan 20–Jan 20, all deportation types) is close to the threshold but covers a different start date and broader scope. Given the conflicting, unverifiable evidence, the question cannot be resolved definitively.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will RFK Jr. announce any preliminary findings on the cause of autism before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
RFK Jr. has been working to identify the cause of autism and has announced that he will release a report in September claiming to have identified 'certain interventions' that are 'clearly almost certainly causing autism' [https://theohiostar.com/2025/08/rfk-jr-says-agency-will-reveal-causes-of-autism-in-september/](https://theohiostar.com/2025/08/rfk-jr-says-agency-will-reveal-causes-of-autism-in-september/). However, he has also walked back his deadline for finding the cause of autism, stating that it will take 'another six months' to gather solid information [https://www.newsweek.com/rfk-jr-walks-back-deadline-finding-cause-autism-1721415](https://www.newsweek.com/rfk-jr-walks-back-deadline-finding-cause-autism-1721415). The current prevalence of autism is one in 31 children, up from one in 36 in 2020 and one in 150 in 2000 [https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/wr/mm7406a1.htm](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/wr/mm7406a1.htm). Sources: 
The Ohio Star
Newsweek
CDC
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if RFK Jr. announces any preliminary findings on the cause of autism between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as reported by credible news sources such as The New York Times [https://www.nytimes.com/](https://www.nytimes.com/), CNN [https://www.cnn.com/](https://www.cnn.com/), or the CDC [https://www.cdc.gov/](https://www.cdc.gov/).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides an indicator of whether RFK Jr. is making progress in identifying the cause of autism. If he announces preliminary findings, it could suggest that he is on track to meet his goal of finding the cause of autism by November 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: RFK Jr. announces any preliminary findings on the cause of autism between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), as reported by credible news sources. Observable evidence needed: explicit news reporting of RFK Jr. presenting findings (even preliminary) on autism causation within the specified window. Key entities: RFK Jr. (HHS Secretary), autism cause findings, credible news sources (NYT, CNN, CDC, or equivalent).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'RFK Jr. autism cause findings announcement 2025' (Sep 1-Oct 1) — to find any autism cause announcement; Query 2: 'RFK Kennedy autism preliminary findings report September 2025' (Sep 1-Oct 1) — to find specific preliminary findings report; Query 3: 'RFK Jr. Trump autism announcement September 22 2025 findings acetaminophen Tylenol' (Sep 22-Oct 1) — to confirm the September 22 event; Query 4: 'RFK Kennedy autism cause announcement White House press conference September 2025' (Sep 22-Oct 1) — to confirm details of the press conference.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 9, 2025 — MAHA report released calling for investigation into autism causes but not presenting findings; this is a call for research, not a finding announcement. (2) September 22, 2025 — Trump and RFK Jr. held a White House press conference in the Roosevelt Room explicitly announcing findings linking prenatal acetaminophen (Tylenol) use to autism risk and announcing leucovorin as a treatment, plus 13 NIH research grants. RFK Jr. stated environmental factors including acetaminophen were causing autism and presented this as their preliminary findings. This is the primary qualifying event. (3) Ongoing verbal claims from RFK Jr. during cabinet meetings (e.g., Aug 26 cabinet meeting where he said interventions 'almost certainly causing autism') — these pre-date the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The September 22, 2025 White House press conference explicitly satisfies the criteria. Per [NBC San Diego](https://www.nbcsandiego.com/news/national-international/trump-administration-charlie-kirk-autism-united-nations/3904393/): 'On Sept. 22 2025, President Donald Trump held a briefing in the White House Roosevelt Room with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr...The briefing announced new findings on children's health, focusing on autism.' Per [AP](https://apnews.com/article/rfk-jr-trump-health-maha-pharma-autism-55db3f5c14a6e3a2aef2483d21ac679b): The MAHA report called for research into autism causes. Per [Mother Jones](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/09/trump-rfk-autism-conference-hhs-tylenol/): 'President Donald Trump and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. held a press conference in which they claimed that Tylenol taken during pregnancy was a leading factor in autism.' Per [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/trump-rfk-autism-paracetamol-vaccines-b2831586.html): 'Donald Trump and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (RFK) have promoted unproven links between acetaminophen (Tylenol), vaccines, and autism, according to a report released by the Department of Health and Human Services.' RFK Jr. stated on record that prenatal acetaminophen use and folate deficiency are causes of autism — this constitutes an announcement of preliminary findings, even if disputed by scientists. The resolution criteria only requires announcing 'any preliminary findings' not that they be scientifically validated.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 22, 2025 at approximately 4:00 PM ET (21:00 UTC), confirmed by PBS 'at 4 p.m. ET' and multiple live-update articles time-stamped September 22, 2025. Exact ISO 8601: 2025-09-22T21:00:00Z (approximate but supported by multiple simultaneous sources).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying announcement of preliminary findings was found within the window. The September 9 MAHA report called for research but did not present findings on causes. The September 22 event is the first formal announcement of preliminary findings within the September 1–October 1 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence considered: (1) Politico reportedly noted 'no HHS report from Kennedy exists ahead of the press conference,' but the press conference itself still occurred and RFK Jr. made oral statements presenting findings — this does not negate the announcement. (2) Scientific experts dispute the validity of the claims (Kenvue, ACOG, FDA, autism advocacy groups), but the resolution criteria require only that RFK Jr. 'announce' findings, not that they be scientifically valid. (3) Multiple credible sources (AP, PBS, NBC, The Independent, AFP, Yahoo News, Mother Jones) all independently confirm the September 22 press conference occurred and included RFK Jr. announcing findings on autism causes. No contradictory evidence about whether the event occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: On September 22, 2025, RFK Jr. participated in a White House press conference and explicitly announced preliminary findings on the cause of autism — specifically linking prenatal acetaminophen (Tylenol) use and folate deficiency to autism risk, and announcing 13 NIH research grants to investigate further. This was reported by multiple credible news sources including AP, PBS, NBC San Diego, The Independent, Mother Jones, and many others. The event falls squarely within the resolution window (September 1 – October 1, 2025). The resolution criteria are satisfied: RFK Jr. announced preliminary findings on the cause of autism within the specified window. Resolution: YES.

The detention order only came on January 21, 2026 — outside the question window. The August 28, 2025 court denial of the arrest warrant confirms there was no prior detention order. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The only detention order for Han Duck-soo found is dated January 21, 2026 (post-verdict immediate detention) — which is AFTER the question window ends on January 18, 2026. No detention warrant was issued for Han Duck-soo within the December 25, 2025 – January 18, 2026 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first (and only) detention order for Han Duck-soo occurred on January 21, 2026, following his conviction. This is after the end of the question window. The August 2025 arrest warrant was denied. No detention warrant was ordered within the question window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources confirm: (1) Han's arrest warrant was denied in August 2025 [Hankyoreh, Korea Herald]. (3) Han continued trial without detention through January 2026 [Chosun.com, Dec 26 article confirms verdict scheduled Jan 21]. evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows that no court ordered a detention warrant for Han Duck-soo between December 25, 2025 and January 18, 2026. subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal budget deficit exceed $1.5 trillion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. national debt has surpassed $37 trillion, with the Congressional Budget Office projecting that federal debt could reach $54 trillion within a decade. The current federal budget deficit is a significant concern, with the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget warning that if the current fiscal trajectory continues, the national debt could exceed $53 trillion by 2035. According to a report by the Congressional Budget Office, the U.S. has accumulated a $2 trillion federal budget deficit over the past 11 months, with the government spending $6.7 trillion and collecting $4.7 trillion in revenues. https://www.cbo.gov/publication/57411. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget has also warned that the national debt is currently as large as the economy and interest costs are surging to record highs. https://www.crfb.org/papers/2025-fiscal-outlook.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. federal budget deficit exceeds $1.5 trillion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19, according to the Congressional Budget Office's daily reports on the federal budget deficit, available at https://www.cbo.gov/publication/daily-budget-deficit. The resolution source will be the Congressional Budget Office's website, and the question will be resolved based on the data available on the website between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19.
subquestions.rationale: The U.S. federal budget deficit is a key indicator of the country's fiscal health, and a large deficit could contribute to an increase in the national debt. If the deficit exceeds $1.5 trillion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19, it could be a sign that the national debt is on track to surpass $38 trillion in 2025. Sources: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/57411, https://www.crfb.org/papers/2025-fiscal-outlook, https://www.cbo.gov/publication/daily-budget-deficit

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The U.S. federal budget deficit must exceed $1.5 trillion as reported by the CBO between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19. Observable evidence: A CBO publication showing a deficit figure >$1.5T during this window. Key entities: CBO, U.S. federal deficit. Threshold: $1.5 trillion. Timing: October 1–19, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'CBO federal budget deficit 2025 fiscal year' (Oct 1–19, 2025) — to find CBO deficit reports within the window. Query 2: 'US federal budget deficit trillion 2025 Congressional Budget Office' (Sep 1–Oct 19, 2025) — to find the FY2025 final deficit figure. Query 3: 'CBO daily budget deficit report October 8 2025 fiscal year 2025' — to confirm the exact release date. Query 4: 'CBO budget deficit $1.809 trillion fiscal year 2025 report' — to verify the exact figure.
evidence.step3_event_detection: CBO released its Monthly Budget Review for FY2025 on October 8, 2025, reporting a deficit of approximately $1.809 trillion for fiscal year 2025 (ended September 30, 2025). This is explicitly stated in multiple sources: Washington Examiner (Oct 8, 2025), Daily Caller (Oct 8, 2025), Fox Business (Oct 10, 2025), AFP (Oct 9, 2025), Fortune (Oct 9, 2025). No conflicting data found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The CBO reported a deficit of $1.809 trillion for FY2025, as published on October 8, 2025 — within the October 1–19 window. $1.809 trillion > $1.5 trillion threshold. Sources: [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance-and-economy/3842795/interest-payments-1-federal-deficit-hit-1-8-fiscal-2025-cbo/), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/cbo-reports-1-8-trillion-federal-deficit-debt-costs-hit-record-1-trillion), [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/10/08/us-budget-deficit-hit-1-8-trillion-in-2025-cbo-reports/), [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/789G79E). All confirm $1.8 trillion+ deficit from CBO.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: CBO published the Monthly Budget Review on October 8, 2025. Multiple sources published on October 8–10, 2025 confirm this. The report was issued on Wednesday, October 8, 2025, within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The CBO report for FY2025 was released on October 8, 2025 — the first such report within the October 1–19 window. There is no earlier CBO publication within the window showing the FY2025 final figure, as the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently report $1.8 trillion (~$1.809 trillion) from CBO for FY2025, published October 8, 2025. No contradictory data exists. The deficit clearly exceeds the $1.5 trillion threshold. The resolution criteria reference 'daily reports on the federal budget deficit' at cbo.gov — the CBO Monthly Budget Review is the standard annual/monthly CBO budget report consistent with this URL pattern. The FY2025 deficit of $1.809 trillion is unambiguously above $1.5 trillion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The CBO published its FY2025 budget deficit figure of $1.809 trillion on October 8, 2025, which is within the October 1–19, 2025 window and exceeds the $1.5 trillion threshold. Multiple high-quality sources confirm this. Resolution: Yes.

question: GPT ads by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI integrates advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model made publicly available by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Limited advertisement releases restricted to a specific region, model, or user group will qualify. The release must be publicly announced as accessible to the relevant users. Closed betas or fully private testing do not count.

Once implemented, the market will resolve to “Yes” immediately, regardless of whether the integration is later removed.

An announcement will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes"; only the release of the advertisement integration will trigger a "Yes" resolution for this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce plans to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT or any successor general-purpose GPT model between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI has been exploring the possibility of introducing advertisements into ChatGPT, as evidenced by code findings in the beta version 1.2025.329 of the Android app, which reference 'ads feature,' 'search ad,' and 'bazaar content' <https://www.engadget.com/code-suggests-openai-may-be-close-to-introducing-ads-for-chatgpt-163024184.html>. The company's CEO, Sam Altman, has expressed discomfort with the idea of ads but has not ruled them out entirely <https://www.tomsguide.com/news/ads-could-soon-be-coming-to-chatgpt-heres-what-we-know>. With the growing user base of ChatGPT, reaching approximately 800 million weekly users <https://www.fudzilla.com/news/ai/57551-openai-plans-to-enshitify-chatgpt-with-adverts>, the introduction of ads could help cover the high operational costs of large AI models while maintaining a free tier. Sources: 
Engadget: https://www.engadget.com/ 
Tom's Guide: https://www.tomsguide.com/ 
Fudzilla: https://www.fudzilla.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if OpenAI officially announces plans to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT or any successor general-purpose GPT model between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05, as reported by credible sources such as The Verge <https://www.theverge.com/> or TechCrunch <https://techcrunch.com/>. The announcement must be publicly available and accessible through OpenAI's official website <https://openai.com/> or reputable news outlets.
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement from OpenAI regarding the integration of advertisements into ChatGPT or any successor general-purpose GPT model would be a significant indicator of the company's plans to monetize its AI technology, which is relevant to the ultimate question of whether GPT ads will be introduced by March 31, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: OpenAI must OFFICIALLY ANNOUNCE PLANS to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT or successor GPT model, between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05, as reported by credible sources like The Verge or TechCrunch. 'Official announcement of plans' means a public, formal statement confirming intent to implement ads — distinct from mere exploration, internal testing, or spokesperson acknowledgment of considering ads. Key entities: OpenAI, ChatGPT. Timing: Dec 6, 2025 – Jan 5, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertisements ads integration announcement' (Dec 6–Jan 5) — to find any official announcement; 2) 'OpenAI advertising revenue model ChatGPT 2025' — to find monetization announcements; 3) 'OpenAI official announcement ads ChatGPT plans confirmed' — to find formal plan declarations; 4) 'OpenAI The Verge TechCrunch advertising ChatGPT announcement' — to find coverage by named credible sources; 5) 'OpenAI Sam Altman advertising announcement press release 2025' — to find formal communications.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Dec 6-8: OpenAI denies live ad tests; Nick Turley says 'There are no live tests for ads'; Mark Chen confirms app promotions turned off — this contradicts a Yes resolution. (B) Dec 9: Adweek reports code strings suggesting ad framework — no official announcement. (C) Dec 25-30: Reports citing The Information that OpenAI is 'exploring' and 'advancing plans' for ads, employees creating mockups — but all sources explicitly state no official announcement was made. (D) OpenAI spokesperson statement 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' — acknowledged exploration, not a formal plan announcement. All candidates rejected as failing to meet the 'official announcement of plans' standard.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require an 'officially announced plan' — not exploration, internal mockups, or acknowledging consideration. Key sources explicitly state OpenAI did NOT officially announce plans: MoneyControl (Dec 26): 'OpenAI has not officially announced an advertising strategy' [https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/openai-continues-exploring-ads-inside-chatgpt-as-user-growth-accelerates-article-13743813.html]; Times of India (Dec 25): 'OpenAI has not publicly announced advertising plans' [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/openai-may-soon-show-ads-inside-chatgpt-employees-reportedly-create-mockups/articleshow/126173586.cms]; The Verge (Dec 8): OpenAI disabled ad-like promotions and denied ads [https://www.theverge.com/news/839882/openai-chatgpt-ads-app-promo-messages-turned-off]; TechCrunch (Dec 7): OpenAI confirmed no live ad tests [https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/07/openai-says-its-turned-off-app-suggestions-that-look-like-ads/]; KnowTechie (Dec 30): 'no rollout date has been announced, and the current status remains prototype-level experimentation' [https://knowtechie.com/openai-chatgpt-ads-exploring/]; Digital Trends (Dec 29): 'No official launch date has been announced' [https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/chatgpt-ads-wont-show-up-in-your-chats-soon-but-openai-is-still-testing-them/]. The OpenAI spokesperson statement 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' is NOT an official announcement of plans — it is merely acknowledging exploration.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred. The closest events (denials of ads on Dec 6-8, exploration reports on Dec 25-30) do not constitute official plan announcements.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found within the window. The window ended Jan 5, 2026 with no official announcement made.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple high-quality sources explicitly state OpenAI did NOT officially announce advertising plans during this window. The Verge and TechCrunch — the specific sources named in the resolution criteria — both covered the story as a denial/exploration, not a formal announcement. OpenAI actively denied live ad tests at the start of the window (Dec 6-8). Reports of internal exploration in late December do not rise to the level of an 'official announcement of plans.' No contradictory evidence suggests a formal announcement was made.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes resolution was NOT met. During Dec 6 – Jan 5, 2026: (1) OpenAI explicitly denied live ad tests on Dec 6-8; (2) Internal exploration/mockups were reported in late December but no official announcement was made; (3) Multiple credible sources including The Verge and TechCrunch — the specific outlets named in the resolution criteria — reported OpenAI was only 'exploring' ads, not announcing plans; (4) The spokesperson statement 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' does not constitute an official announcement of plans. Resolution: No. The window closed on Jan 5, 2026 with no qualifying announcement.

subquestions.question: Will the number of reported ceasefire violations in Ukraine decrease by at least 20% between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11, compared to the preceding month?
subquestions.background_information: The conflict in Ukraine has been ongoing since 2014, with a significant escalation in 2022. Recent efforts by President Trump to broker a ceasefire have shown promise, but the situation remains volatile. According to the OSCE, there were over 10,000 ceasefire violations reported in October 2025. A decrease in ceasefire violations would indicate a positive trend towards peace. Sources: OSCE: https://www.osce.org/ BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-64631115
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the number of reported ceasefire violations in Ukraine, as reported by the OSCE, decreases by at least 20% between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11, compared to the preceding month. The data will be obtained from the OSCE's official website. In case the OSCE website is unavailable, alternative sources such as BBC News will be used.
subquestions.rationale: A decrease in ceasefire violations in Ukraine would indicate a positive trend towards peace, which is relevant to the ultimate question of whether any major conflicts or events will occur between September 10, 2025, and December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OSCE reports showing ≥20% decrease in ceasefire violations in Ukraine between Nov 11–Dec 11, 2025, vs. Oct 11–Nov 11, 2025. Observable evidence: numerical ceasefire violation counts from OSCE official website for both periods. Key entities: OSCE, Ukraine ceasefire violations. Threshold: 20% reduction. Timing: Nov 11–Dec 11, 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OSCE ceasefire violations Ukraine 2025' — to find current monitoring data; 2) 'OSCE Ukraine monitoring mission ceasefire report November December 2025' — to find specific reports; 3) 'OSCE Special Monitoring Mission SMM Ukraine terminated 2022' — to confirm mission status; 4) 'Ukraine ceasefire violations count decrease November December 2025' — to find any numerical data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events found providing OSCE ceasefire violation statistics for Ukraine in Nov–Dec 2025. Multiple articles discuss OSCE's *potential future* monitoring role. The OSCE SMM was terminated in 2022. Articles reference the OSCE preparing contingency plans but not actively monitoring violations. No numerical ceasefire violation data from OSCE found for either the comparison period or the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria cannot be matched because the underlying data source does not exist. The OSCE's SMM — the body that would generate ceasefire violation reports for Ukraine — was terminated in 2022 after Russia vetoed its mandate renewal [SWI swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/foreign-affairs/no-peacewithout-oversight-monitoring-ukraines-ceasefire/89285618). Multiple late-2025 sources confirm OSCE is planning for *future* potential ceasefire monitoring but has no active mission generating this data [AA.com.tr](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/osce-ready-to-assume-responsibilities-if-ukraine-ceasefire-achieved/3762631). The resolution criteria specifies OSCE data which is unavailable.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no OSCE ceasefire violation statistical report for Ukraine exists in the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found at all.
evidence.step7_verification: Verified from multiple independent sources (SWI, AFP, TASS, Anadolu Agency, Asia Times) that the OSCE SMM in Ukraine was terminated in 2022 and no replacement monitoring mission has been established. The war is ongoing with heavy fighting. The UN Security Council reports escalating civilian casualties in November–December 2025, directly contradicting any notion of reduced conflict intensity. Civilian deaths in Jan–Nov 2025 were 24% higher than the same period in 2024 per UN data.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question is unresolvable because the underlying data source (OSCE ceasefire violation reports for Ukraine) does not exist. The OSCE's Special Monitoring Mission was terminated in 2022. No new monitoring mission has been established. The resolution criteria specifies OSCE data, which is unavailable. The alternative source (BBC News) also would not have OSCE-specific numerical ceasefire violation statistics. The question cannot be resolved Yes or No with verifiable evidence.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be at least 5 reported incidents of Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent incidents have shown an increase in Russian military activity near NATO borders. On September 10, 2025, 19 Russian drones entered Polish airspace, prompting a response from NATO air defenses (https://www.columbustelegram.com/news/incursion-injects-fear/article_4fbaa3c2-55a4-11ec-9f7a-83b8d591751b.html). This incident has raised concerns about the potential for further escalation. According to NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg, air policing has surged fourfold since Russia’s Ukraine invasion (https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/nato-scrambles-fighter-jets-face-28874145). The European Union’s foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, has warned that the incursion could be a 'game changer' and called for stronger sanctions (https://apnews.com/article/europe-russia-ukraine-poland-nato-3b8fbd94e5a14d9fbfbd9c5e5c5a16d5). Sources: 
Columbus Telegram: https://www.columbustelegram.com/news/incursion-injects-fear/article_4fbaa3c2-55a4-11ec-9f7a-83b8d591751b.html 
Mirror: https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/nato-scrambles-fighter-jets-face-28874145 
AP News: https://apnews.com/article/europe-russia-ukraine-poland-nato-3b8fbd94e5a14d9fbfbd9c5e5c5a16d5
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least 5 reported incidents of Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace occur between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24, as reported by credible news sources such as NATO (https://www.nato.int/), the European Union (https://europa.eu/), or reputable news agencies like AP News (https://apnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because an increase in reported incidents of Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace could indicate a higher likelihood of a military clash between NATO and Russia. The resolution of this question could provide insight into the current level of tension and the potential for further escalation.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least 5 reported incidents of Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace between 2025-09-24T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-24T23:59:59Z, as reported by credible sources (NATO, EU, or reputable news agencies). Observable evidence: News articles explicitly reporting Russian aircraft/drones entering specific NATO member state airspace within the window. Key threshold: 5 separate incidents. Key entities: Russian military aircraft, Russian drones, NATO member state airspace.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russian military aircraft NATO airspace violation 2025' (Sept-Oct) — to find all incidents; 2) 'Russian drone NATO airspace incursion October 2025' — to find drone-specific events; 3) 'Russian drones Polish airspace October 2025 NATO incident' — to find Poland-specific events; 4) 'Estonia MiG-31 airspace violation September 19 2025' — to identify the Estonian incident timing; 5) 'Russian drones Romania Lithuania Sweden airspace violation October 2025' — to find additional incidents; 6) 'Russia NATO airspace incursion list all incidents September October 2025' — comprehensive list; 7) 'Russian drones Polish airspace October 13 2025 shot down' — specific October incident; 8) 'Denmark Sweden Norway Russian drone airspace October 2025 confirmed NATO member' — to find Nordic incidents.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Estonia MiG-31 incident: Sept 19, 2025 — REJECTED as BEFORE the window start (Sept 24). (B) Copenhagen/Danish airports drone incidents: Multiple sources confirm drone activity at Danish airports around Sept 22-29, with Copenhagen Airport closed Sept 23 and ongoing incidents Sept 25-29. Some incidents straddle the window boundary; Sept 24 onwards clearly within window. (C) Germany: Russian aircraft buzzed German frigate Sept 24, 2025 — confirmed by German Defense Minister published Sept 25; within window. (D) Sweden Karlskrona naval base drones: Sept 26, 2025 — within window. (E) Norway drone incidents: Multiple during late September and October — some attributable to Russia per Norwegian PM. (F) Romania drone: Sept 13 — REJECTED as before the window. (G) Poland drone incident Oct 13, 2025: Over 20 Russian drones entered Polish airspace, NATO jets responded — confirmed by multiple sources; within window. (H) Lithuania Su-30/Il-78 incident: Oct 23, 2025 — confirmed by Lithuanian military, AFP, PBS, NATO; within window. (I) Danish airports further drone incidents (late September): Multiple confirmed within window. (J) Lithuanian drone incidents (July/summer 2025): REJECTED as before the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Confirmed incidents within the window that clearly match the criteria (Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace, credibly reported): 1) Denmark/Danish airports — drone activity Sept 24-29, 2025, attributed to Russia by Danish PM. [Yahoo/multiple sources](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/two-russian-military-aircraft-enter-181252621.html) references 'Copenhagen Airport closed due to drone sightings on September 23, 2025' plus ongoing incidents. 2) Sweden Karlskrona — Russian-attributed drones near naval base Sept 26 [Firstpost](https://www.firstpost.com/world/after-denmark-and-norway-drones-near-swedish-naval-base-set-off-alarm-bells-ws-e-13937244.html). 3) Germany frigate — Russian aircraft buzzed German navy frigate on Sept 24 per German Defense Minister [Aerotime](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/germany-accuses-russian-aircraft-of-buzzing-navy-frigate) — NOTE: buzzing a frigate in the Baltic Sea may not constitute 'entering NATO airspace' per se (international waters). This incident is less clearly meeting the airspace criteria. 4) Poland Oct 13 — over 20 Russian drones entered Polish airspace, NATO jets responded per [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/russian-fighter-jets-breach-nato-member-lithuanias-airspace-as-war-with-ukraine-continues-what-happened-next/articleshow/124768718.cms) and [Notes From Poland](https://notesfrompoland.com/2025/10/17/how-have-the-russian-drone-incursions-affected-polish-politics/). 5) Lithuania Oct 23 — Su-30+Il-78 in Lithuanian airspace 18 seconds per [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/79U6863), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/president-of-lithuania-says-russian-military-planes-violated-countrys-airspace), [RFERL](https://www.rferl.org/a/lithuania-russia-ukraine-airspace-violation-nauseda-sukhoi/33568796.html). Additionally, the European Parliament resolution (Oct 9) cites 'repeated drone breaches of Lithuanian, Romanian, and Hungarian airspace' as recent events. The EP resolution (B10-0437/2025, Oct 7) cites 25 September 2025: 'five Russian jets were intercepted near NATO airspace' — but 'near' is ambiguous. Denmark's multiple airport drone closures (starting Sept 23, continuing through late September/early October) represent multiple separate incidents. Norway's drone incidents over military bases also reported within the window. Incidents 1, 2, 4, and 5 alone yield 4 confirmed violations of NATO sovereign airspace; with Denmark/Norway incidents clearly adding more. The total number of confirmed, credibly-reported incidents within the window substantially exceeds 5.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Incident 1 (Denmark drones): Multiple incidents Sept 24-29, first clearly within window around Sept 24 onwards; Copenhagen closure on Sept 23/24. Incident 2 (Sweden Karlskrona): Sept 26, 2025. Incident 3 (Poland Oct 13): October 13, 2025 (exact date confirmed by Economic Times). Incident 4 (Lithuania Oct 23): October 23, 2025, approximately 1600 CET (=1500 UTC), confirmed across multiple sources with exact timestamps.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question only requires whether 5 or more incidents occurred within the window, not whether a 'first occurrence' applies. By the time of Lithuania's Oct 23 incident, already at least 4 earlier qualifying incidents within the window had been reported. The 5th qualifying incident (Lithuania Oct 23) clearly falls within the window. Actually, incidents within the window accumulate to well more than 5 — Poland Oct 13 alone counted as one incident; Denmark (multiple incidents Sept 24-29); Sweden Sept 26; Norway (multiple during window); Lithuania Oct 23 = at minimum 5 separate incidents.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some sources note Russia denied all violations. Some Danish/Norwegian/German drone sightings remain unattributed with certainty. However, the Poland Oct 13 incident (20+ drones in Polish airspace, NATO jets responding) and Lithuania Oct 23 (Su-30/Il-78 in Lithuanian airspace, Lithuanian military confirmed, NATO responded) are definitively confirmed. The EP resolution (Oct 9) explicitly lists Russia as responsible for multiple confirmed airspace violations within this period. The Arms Control Association article confirms the Sept 10 drones over Poland ('largest-scale incursion') — but Sept 10 is before the window. The key Poland Oct 13 incident needs further verification: the Economic Times article states 'on October 13, 2025, over 20 Russian drones entered Polish airspace, with NATO jets shooting down some'. The Notes From Poland article (Oct 17) also confirms 'Russian drone incursions into Polish airspace in October 2025, primarily originating from Belarus.' This confirms an October 2025 Poland incident distinct from the Sept 10 one. With Poland (Oct 13) + Lithuania (Oct 23) + Denmark (Sept 24-29 multiple) + Sweden (Sept 26) + Norway (multiple), the total exceeds 5 definitively.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows at least 5 reported incidents of Russian military aircraft or drones entering NATO airspace between Sept 24 and Oct 24, 2025. The most explicitly confirmed incidents include: (1) Danish airspace drone incidents (late Sept, starting around Sept 24, attributed to Russia by Danish PM); (2) Sweden Karlskrona naval base drones Sept 26; (3) Norway drone incidents (multiple, confirmed by Norwegian PM as unacceptable); (4) Poland Oct 13 — 20+ Russian drones in Polish airspace (NATO jets responded); (5) Lithuania Oct 23 — two Russian military aircraft in Lithuanian airspace (Su-30 + Il-78, confirmed by Lithuanian military, AFP, PBS, NATO). Multiple credible sources including AFP, PBS, RFERL, Lithuanian military, Economic Times, Notes from Poland, and the European Parliament all confirm these incidents. The threshold of 5 incidents is definitively met. The question resolves Yes. The 5th qualifying incident (Lithuania Oct 23) establishes the final confirmation, though the threshold was likely met well before that date (by the Poland Oct 13 incident, with Denmark/Norway/Sweden incidents earlier in the window). The resolution datetime is best assigned to Oct 13, 2025 when the Poland drone incident (clearly the 5th or later incident) was reported, though conservative attribution places it no later than Oct 23 when Lithuania was confirmed. subquestions.question: Will Congress pass a continuing resolution or a new appropriations bill for fiscal year 2026 by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. federal funding cycle ends at midnight on September 30, 2025, and a partial government shutdown could begin on October 1 if Congress fails to pass new appropriations. According to an article by Military Times, Congress faces a looming partial government shutdown if a new budget or short-term extension is not passed by September 30. The article notes that the last major shutdown occurred in December 2018, lasting 35 days. Another article by New Hampshire Bulletin reports that Congress is facing a high risk of a government shutdown on October 1, 2025, because it has failed to pass the dozen full-year appropriations bills that fund about one-third of federal spending. Sources: https://www.militarytimes.com/ https://newhampshirebulletin.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Congress passes a continuing resolution or a new appropriations bill for fiscal year 2026 between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-01, as reported by official government sources such as the Congress.gov website or the White House website. The resolution source will be the official government websites, which will be checked for announcements of passed legislation.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it addresses the immediate cause of a potential government shutdown. If Congress passes a continuing resolution or a new appropriations bill, it would prevent a shutdown, while a failure to do so would increase the likelihood of a shutdown.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Congress must PASS (both chambers) a continuing resolution OR a new appropriations bill for fiscal year 2026 between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Observable evidence: signed legislation or congressional passage record on congress.gov or whitehouse.gov. Key entities: U.S. Congress (House + Senate), FY2026 appropriations or CR. Timing: window ends at 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Congress continuing resolution fiscal year 2026 passed' (2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01) — to find any passed legislation. Query 2: 'government shutdown October 2025 appropriations bill' (2025-09-17 to 2025-10-01) — to find shutdown evidence or avoidance. Query 3: 'government shutdown October 1 2025 started began' — to confirm shutdown occurrence. Query 4: 'Senate vote continuing resolution September 30 2025 failed passed' — to confirm final legislative outcome.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) House passed CR (H.R. 5371) on September 19, 2025 (217-212) — REJECTED as qualifying event because only ONE chamber passed it; Senate did not pass it. (2) Senate voted on House-passed CR on September 30, 2025 — failed 55-45 (did not meet 60-vote threshold). (3) Senate voted on Democrat-led CR (S. 2882) on September 30, 2025 — failed 53-47. (4) Government shutdown began October 1, 2025 — confirmed by multiple sources including Daily Signal, Fox2Detroit, Politomix/Guardian. No CR or appropriations bill was passed by BOTH chambers within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require Congress (both chambers) to PASS a CR or appropriations bill. Evidence shows: [CSIS analysis](https://www.csis.org/analysis/what-government-shutdown-would-mean-defense-funding-fy-2026) states 'Congress has not finalized defense funding: the House passed its defense appropriations bill, but the Senate has not voted on its version.' [JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/government-shutdown-advisory-summary-of-7789664/) confirms 'no FY 2026 appropriations bills have been enacted.' [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/us/government-on-brink-of-shutdown-after-senate-blocks-gop-stopgap-funding-bill-5922256) reports 'The federal government is on the brink of a shutdown... after the U.S. Senate rejected two temporary funding bills.' [Daily Signal](https://www.dailysignal.com/2025/10/01/amid-shutdown-republicans-seek-soften-democrat-resistance/) reports 'Amid Shutdown' on October 1, 2025. [Politomix/Guardian](https://politomix.com/the-guardian/2293120/us-government-shuts-down-after-democrats-refuse-to-back/) states 'The U.S. government shut down on October 1, 2025.' This definitively shows no CR or appropriations bill was passed by both chambers within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The shutdown began at 12:01 AM Eastern Time on October 1, 2025, which is 2025-10-01T04:01:00Z. The Senate's final vote rejecting the Republican CR occurred on September 30, 2025 at approximately 5:30 PM EDT (2025-09-30T21:30:00Z), which is the last legislative action. Both bills failed before the deadline. The definitive 'No' moment is when the last Senate vote failed on September 30, 2025, before midnight.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence (passage of a CR or FY2026 appropriations bill by both chambers) exists within the window. The House passed H.R. 5371 on September 19, but the Senate failed to pass it on the same day and again on September 30. No other legislation passed both chambers. The condition was definitively not met.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources confirm the shutdown began October 1, 2025: Daily Signal, Fox2Detroit, Politomix/Guardian, Washington Examiner, Townhall, Epoch Times, CSIS. All sources agree both Senate votes failed on September 30, 2025. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a CR was passed. The CSIS article dated September 30 explicitly states 'Congress has not finalized defense funding' and describes the scenario where 'a government shutdown is likely.' The Daily Signal article from October 1 is 'Amid Shutdown' — confirming shutdown in effect. There is no evidence of any last-minute deal before the October 1 midnight deadline.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. Congress did NOT pass a continuing resolution or new appropriations bill for FY2026 by October 1, 2025. The House passed H.R. 5371 on September 19, 2025, but the Senate failed it twice — on September 19 and again on September 30, 2025 (55-45, failing to reach 60-vote threshold). The Democratic CR also failed (53-47). The government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, at 12:01 AM ET. The definitive No moment is the end of the resolution window (2025-10-01T23:59:59Z), as the shutdown was already underway but Congress could theoretically have passed something on October 1 within the window. However, evidence from October 1 shows the shutdown was ongoing with no deal reached. The resolution_datetime is set to 2025-10-01T04:01:00Z when the shutdown formally began, confirming no CR was passed.

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Key timestamp: September 15, 2025 — Azov Corps announced liberation of Pankivka (Ukraine captured it, driving Russians out). This is the opposite of what the question asks about. No timestamp found for Russian capture of Pankivka.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (Russian capture of Pankivka) found at any point in the September 1-25, 2025 window. Therefore, no first occurrence to verify.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks if Russian forces will capture Pankivka between September 1-25, 2025. evidence.step8_final_decision: The domestic gross of A Minecraft Movie was approximately $423.9 million before September 1, 2025, and remained at approximately $423.9-424 million through late September 2025. evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Israeli government officially announces plans to annex any part of the West Bank between 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-02. Must be announced by PM or FM. Trump publicly stated on Sept 25-26 he would 'not allow' annexation [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-says-he-wont-let-israel-annex-the-west-bank/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/26/trump-says-he-will-not-allow-israel-to-annex-occupied-west-bank/). evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence found. The only possible candidate (Sa'ar's reported statement to Rubio on/before Sept 2) is (1) from secondary reporting via Walla, not a formal official announcement, and (2) contradicted by Sa'ar's own Sept 25 statement ruling out annexation of population centers.

The overall picture is that while annexation was discussed and proposed by coalition members, the Israeli government (PM Netanyahu, FM Sa'ar) did NOT officially announce plans to annex. evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. Throughout the window, while there were proposals and calls for annexation from Finance Minister Smotrich and other right-wing ministers, the Israeli government (PM Netanyahu / FM Sa'ar) did not officially announce plans to annex any part of the West Bank. The window closed Oct 2 without an official government announcement meeting the criteria.

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.
