[AP](https://apnews.com/article/brazil-bolsonaro-coup-trial-513fff1adc42b1ff60754eb2ab0f29ae). The Globe and Mail article from Sept 11 confirms: 'Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro was convicted by a majority of the Supreme Court on **Thursday**' (Sept 11) [Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-former-brazil-president-bolsonaro-guilty-of-coup-charges-supreme-court/). TASS from Sept 11: 'The Federal Supreme Court of Brazil convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro...according to a ruling released on **September 11, 2025**.' The actual ruling was on Sept 11, outside the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The final ruling/verdict was announced on September 11, 2025 — explicitly outside the resolution window of Sept 1-9. On September 9 (last day of window), only two of five justices had voted, and proceedings were adjourned.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying earlier occurrence (complete ruling) was found within the Sept 1-9 window. The voting process began Sept 9 but no final ruling was issued on that date.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (AP, TASS, Globe and Mail, Newser, Devdiscourse) all confirm the final conviction ruling was announced on September 11, 2025. The Sept 9 session resulted in only partial votes (2 of 5 justices) with adjournment. No contradictory evidence suggests a final ruling was issued on or before Sept 9.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Brazilian Supreme Court began deliberations on September 9 (within the window), but only two of five justices voted on that day and the case was adjourned. The actual ruling/verdict was announced on September 11, 2025 — outside the resolution window of September 1-9. Therefore, the question resolves No. The window closed on September 9, 2025 without a final ruling being announced.

question: Will any of the stolen Louvre jewels be returned by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any of the jewels stolen from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon are officially recovered by the listed date ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

A single item (e.g., one earring) will suffice regardless of if it is missing a diamond or other element; however, recovery of only a fragment or part of an item (for example, a loose stone or a piece of a crown) will not suffice

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Louvre or the French government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the French authorities announce the recovery of at least one stolen Louvre jewel or the arrest of at least one suspect in connection with the heist between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20?
subquestions.background_information: The Louvre Museum in Paris was robbed of eight historic crown jewels on October 19, 2025, in a daring daylight heist. The stolen items include a sapphire diadem, necklace, and earring set, an emerald necklace and earrings, a reliquary brooch, Empress Eugénie's diadem, and her large corsage-bow brooch. The French government has launched an investigation and is working to recover the stolen items. According to Chris Marinello, CEO of Art Recovery International, the thieves will likely dismantle the jewels and melt down the metal to hide evidence, making recovery unlikely after 24 to 48 hours <https://people.com/crime/expert-says-stolen-louvre-jewels-need-to-be-recovered-in-24-to-48-hours-or-theyre-long-gone/>. The French Ministry of Culture has confirmed that the investigation is ongoing and that no injuries occurred during the incident <https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20251020-louvre-museum-robbed-of-historic-crown-jewels-in-daylight-heist>.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the French authorities announce the recovery of at least one stolen Louvre jewel or the arrest of at least one suspect in connection with the heist between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20, as reported by credible news sources such as France 24 <https://www.france24.com/> or Le Parisien <https://www.leparisien.fr/>. The resolution will be based on official statements from the French government or the Louvre Museum, as well as reports from reputable news outlets.
subquestions.rationale: The recovery of at least one stolen Louvre jewel or the arrest of at least one suspect in connection with the heist would be a significant development in the investigation and could indicate that the authorities are making progress in solving the case. This, in turn, could increase the likelihood of recovering the stolen jewels, which is the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Yes condition: French authorities announce (1) recovery of at least one stolen Louvre jewel OR (2) arrest of at least one suspect in connection with the Louvre heist. Window: 2025-10-21T00:00:00Z to 2025-11-20T23:59:59Z. Key entities: French authorities, Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau, Louvre Museum, stolen crown jewels (heist on October 19, 2025). Observable evidence: credible news reports of official announcement of arrest or recovery within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Louvre jewel heist theft stolen jewelry 2025' (Jan–Nov 2025) — to find background on the heist and any developments. Query 2: 'Louvre museum robbery arrest suspect recovery France 2025' (Oct–Nov 2025) — to find specific arrest/recovery events. Query 3: 'Louvre heist suspects arrested charged November 2025' (Oct 21–Nov 20, 2025) — to confirm events within the window. Query 4: 'Louvre jewels recovered stolen crown France arrest 2025' (Oct 21–Nov 20, 2025) — to look for recovery events.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Two suspects arrested on October 25, 2025, announced October 26, 2025 by Paris Prosecutor Laure Beccuau — within window. (2) Five additional suspects arrested October 29, 2025 — within window. (3) Four suspects formally charged by November 1, 2025 — within window. (4) Empress Eugénie's crown found damaged near the museum — recovery date ambiguous (possibly October 19, the day of the heist, which is BEFORE the window), but the announcements about it appeared within the window. No events rejected; the arrest events are clearly within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The arrest of at least one suspect is confirmed. Paris Prosecutor Laure Beccuau announced on October 26, 2025, that suspects had been arrested on October 25, 2025, in connection with the Louvre jewel heist. [AFP/CBC News](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/paris-louvre-robbery-arrests-9.6954070), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/suspects-arrested-over-theft-of-crown-jewels-from-the-louvre-prosecutor-says), [China Daily](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/27/WS68fe66c4a310f735438b704b.html). This directly matches 'arrest of at least one suspect in connection with the heist' as required by the resolution criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The arrests occurred on October 25, 2025 (Saturday evening), confirmed by Paris Prosecutor on October 26, 2025. This is the first occurrence of a qualifying arrest within the window (October 21–November 20, 2025). The heist itself occurred October 19, 2025, before the window. No arrests are reported between October 19 and October 25 that might constitute an earlier qualifying event before the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying arrest: October 25, 2025 (Saturday evening, local Paris time), publicly confirmed by Paris Prosecutor Laure Beccuau on October 26, 2025. Multiple sources confirm the date. Exact time reported as 'around 10 p.m. local time' at Charles de Gaulle Airport on October 25, 2025 [SBS News](https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/two-suspects-arrested-after-louvre-jewel-heist/3x6pk4vde). This translates to approximately 2025-10-25T21:00:00Z (Paris is UTC+2 in October).
evidence.step7_verification: Verification: Multiple high-credibility sources (AFP, CBC News, PBS, Deutsche Welle, NBC, The Independent, Le Parisien as cited) all confirm arrests of suspects within the resolution window. No contradictory evidence suggesting arrests did not occur. The arrests are clearly within the window (Oct 25, announced Oct 26, 2025 — well within Oct 21 to Nov 20, 2025). One source notes Empress Eugénie's crown was recovered near the museum, but this appears to have occurred on October 19 (day of heist), before the window — however, this doesn't affect resolution since the arrest criterion is independently satisfied.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria are clearly satisfied. The first qualifying event — the arrest of at least one (in fact, two) suspects in connection with the Louvre heist — occurred on October 25, 2025 (within the window of October 21–November 20, 2025) and was officially announced by Paris Prosecutor Laure Beccuau on October 26, 2025. This was widely reported by credible sources including AFP, Le Parisien, CBC News, PBS, Deutsche Welle, and many others. Resolution: YES.

question: U.S. x Iran Military Engagement by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Iran between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Iranian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Iranian land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage.

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; the Iranian Law Enforcement Command is a branch of the Iranian Armed Forces; all sub-branches of the Artesh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (including the Basij), and Law Enforcement Command are part of the Iranian Armed forces.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will there be exactly 1 earthquake of magnitude 7.0 or higher worldwide by December 31?
description:

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. subquestions.question: Will the number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 5.0 or higher in the Pacific Ring of Fire be at least 5 between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09?

According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the region has experienced a significant number of earthquakes in recent months, including a magnitude 8.8 earthquake in July 2025. The USGS also forecasts a 24% chance of another magnitude 7 or higher earthquake in the months ahead, with a greater than 99% probability of continued magnitude 4.0+, 5.0+, and even M6.0+ events over the first year. As of October 2025, there have been several earthquakes in the region, including a magnitude 6.7 earthquake in the Banda Sea and a magnitude 5.6 earthquake near Vilyuchinsk in Russia. [1] https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef, [2] https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-1751219
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 5.0 or higher in the Pacific Ring of Fire is at least 5 between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09, according to the USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef). The USGS Earthquake Notification Service (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/ens/) will be used to track earthquakes in the region.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because the number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 5.0 or higher in the Pacific Ring of Fire can be an indicator of increased seismic activity, which may increase the likelihood of an earthquake with a magnitude of 7.0 or higher occurring in the region. If the number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 5.0 or higher is high, it may suggest that the region is experiencing a period of increased seismic activity, which could increase the likelihood of a larger earthquake occurring.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least 5 earthquakes with magnitude ≥5.0 occurring in the Pacific Ring of Fire between 2025-11-13T00:00:00Z and 2025-12-09T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: USGS/seismological agency reports of M≥5.0 events in Ring of Fire locations (Japan, Indonesia, Philippines, Alaska, Chile, New Zealand, etc.).

evidence.step3_event_detection: Identified 25+ qualifying events. Key confirmed events (all in Pacific Ring of Fire): (1) M5.1 near Kamisu, Ibaraki, Japan, Nov 13, 2025; (2) M5.0 near Ishigaki, Japan, Nov 13, 2025; (3) M5.3 North Pacific Ocean off Iwate, Japan, Nov 13/14, 2025; (4) M6.0 near Tonga and M5.2 near Vallenar Chile, Nov 15, 2025 (per World Eq Report); (5) M5.3 near Hachinohe, Aomori, Japan, Nov 18, 2025; (6) M5.7 off Kamchatka, Russia, Nov 22, 2025; (7) M5.0 near Kenai, Alaska, Nov 22, 2025; (8) M5.9 Mindanao, Philippines, Nov 25, 2025; (9) M5.7/5.8 Kumamoto, Japan, Nov 25, 2025; (10) M5.0 North Pacific near Kamchatka, Nov 26, 2025; (11) M6.6 Simeulue, Indonesia, Nov 27, 2025; (12) M5.8 near Anchorage, Alaska, Nov 27, 2025; (13) M6.0 near Susitna, Alaska, Nov 28, 2025; (14) M5.8 South Pacific near NZ, Dec 1, 2025; (15) M5.4 Solomon Islands, Dec 1, 2025; (16) M5.2 Peru, Dec 1, 2025; (17) M5.6 Banda Sea, Indonesia, Dec 3, 2025; (18) M7.0 Yakutat Alaska, Dec 6, 2025; (19) M7.6 off northeast Japan, Dec 8, 2025; (20) M7.5 off Aomori Japan, Dec 9, 2025. None rejected — all clearly ≥5.0 in Ring of Fire and within window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources confirm well over 5 earthquakes ≥M5.0 in Ring of Fire in the window. On Nov 13 alone: M5.1 near Kamisu, Japan [VolcanoDiscovery](https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquakes/quake-info/22386883/info.html); M5.0 near Ishigaki, Japan [VolcanoDiscovery](https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquake/news/286875/Significant-earthquake-of-magnitude-50-just-reported-30-km-northeast-of-Ishigaki-Japan.html); M5.3/5.6 North Pacific off Iwate, Japan [VolcanoDiscovery](https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquakes/quake-info/22390251/info.html). By Nov 15 the World Earthquake Report already documents additional M5.0+ events in Tonga and Chile [VolcanoDiscovery](https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquake/news/286997/World-Earthquake-Report-for-Saturday-15-November-2025.html). The threshold of 5 was met on or very shortly after Nov 13.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The first qualifying event was M5.1 near Kamisu, Ibaraki, Japan on 2025-11-13 at 09:54 am JST = 2025-11-13T00:54:00Z. The fifth qualifying event (to meet the threshold) was also on Nov 13 or shortly after — the World Earthquake Report for Nov 14 alone documents '2 quakes of magnitude 5.0+' in 24 hours in the Pacific, and the Nov 15 report shows 7 quakes M5.0+ globally. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable in the traditional sense — the question requires an accumulated count of ≥5. The resolution question asks about ≥5 events in the entire 26-day window; typical daily rate of M5.0+ earthquakes globally is ~5-10 per day with majority in Ring of Fire, making it virtually certain the threshold was met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes — the condition is met by a very wide margin. At least 5 earthquakes ≥M5.0 occurred in the Pacific Ring of Fire within the window. Confirmed examples: (1) M5.1 Kamisu, Japan Nov 13; (2) M5.0 Ishigaki, Japan Nov 13; (3) M5.3 North Pacific off Iwate, Japan Nov 13-14; (4) M6.0 Tonga area Nov 15; (5) M5.2 near Vallenar, Chile Nov 15 — all within the first 3 days of the window. Dozens more followed throughout Nov 16 – Dec 9. The threshold of 5 is clearly and unambiguously met.

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any bill with the effect of banning sitting members of the US congress from trading stocks is signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least 100 members of the US House of Representatives sign the discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The End Congressional Stock Trading Act, introduced by Rep. Tim Burchett, aims to prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, and other complex investment vehicles. Currently, there is a growing concern about insider trading among lawmakers, with some achieving high returns on their trades, such as Rep. Nancy Pelosi's estimated 54% portfolio return in 2024. The discharge petition, filed by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, requires 218 signatures to force the bill to the floor. According to Rep. Luna, 'No one sent to Congress should be enriching themselves through Wall Street while writing the very laws that regulate our markets.' [1](https://www.oann.com/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/). The petition has gained support from President Donald Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who stated that 'People shouldn’t come to Washington to get rich, they should come to serve the American people.' [2](https://ktxs.com/news/nation-world/treasury-secretary-backs-push-to-ban-lawmakers-from-trading-stocks). Sources: 
One America News Network: https://www.oann.com/ 
ktxs.com: https://ktxs.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least 100 members of the US House of Representatives sign the discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, as reported by official government sources, such as the US House of Representatives website [https://www.house.gov/](https://www.house.gov/), or credible news outlets, including One America News Network [https://www.oann.com/](https://www.oann.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The number of signatures on the discharge petition is a key indicator of the level of support for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act among members of the US House of Representatives. If a significant number of members sign the petition, it could increase the likelihood of the bill being brought to the floor and ultimately passed, which would be a crucial step towards banning congressional stock trading.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: At least 100 members of the US House must sign the discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908 / Rep. Luna's petition) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: Official House records or credible news reporting stating 100+ signatures on this specific petition. Key entities: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (FL), the End Congressional Stock Trading Act, the discharge petition filed ~August 29-30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition House Representatives' (Aug-Oct 2025) — to find the petition's origin and status. 2) 'discharge petition congressional stock trading ban 2025' (Aug-Oct 2025) — to find any signature count updates. 3) 'Luna discharge petition signatures stock trading ban September 2025' (Sep-Oct 2025) — to find specific counts. 4) 'congressional stock trading discharge petition signatures count 100' (Sep 2025) — to directly check if 100-signature threshold was reported. 5) 'Luna stock trading ban discharge petition abandoned withdrawn September 2025' — to check if petition was dropped.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Luna filed the discharge petition on ~August 29-30, 2025. (2) By September 3-5, reports show she was pursuing 'regular order' after meeting with Speaker Johnson, suggesting she may not be actively collecting signatures. (3) No article reports any specific signature count for the stock trading discharge petition. (4) Separate Epstein files discharge petition reached 217 signatures — this is a different petition entirely. The stock trading petition's signature count is never mentioned in any article.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly states that 100 or more members signed the End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition between September 1-October 1, 2025. Multiple articles from September 3-5 indicate that Luna was pivoting to seek regular order through committee, which would make the discharge petition less actively pursued. Articles from September 19 and later still reference the discharge petition as a potential tool, but no signature counts are reported. The September 5 Semafor article states Luna 'thinks the measure will be sent through regular order for markup' after speaking with Johnson — suggesting the discharge petition was held in abeyance. No source reports 100 signatures on the stock trading petition.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for 100 signatures being reached on the stock trading discharge petition, because no such event is reported in any available source.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (100 signatures on the End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition) found in any source during the September 1 - October 1, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove: searched for the petition being withdrawn/abandoned; searched for any signature counts; searched for any reporting on the petition's progress. The absence of any signature count reporting — combined with Luna's apparent pivot to seeking regular order through committee — strongly suggests the petition did not reach 100 signatures. No contradictory evidence found. The Epstein files petition is a separate petition not relevant to this question.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No evidence exists that 100 members signed the End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition between September 1 and October 1, 2025. All available reporting indicates the petition was filed but Luna pivoted to seeking regular order through Speaker Johnson; no signature counts were ever publicly reported for this petition. The window closed (October 1) with no qualifying event documented. Resolution is No, with resolution_datetime set to 2025-10-01T23:59:59Z as the window closed without a qualifying event.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC report at least 100 new measles cases in the United States between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The CDC has been tracking measles cases in the United States, and as of November 13, 2025, there were 1,723 confirmed cases nationwide, with 87% linked to 45 outbreaks. The current measles outbreak is largely driven by declining vaccination rates, with only 92.5% of children in kindergarten having received the required two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine. According to the CDC, measles is a highly contagious virus that can be prevented through vaccination. The CDC recommends that children receive the MMR vaccine at 12-15 months and 4-6 years old. For more information, see the CDC's measles webpage: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/index.html. Sources: 
https://www.cdc.gov/measles/index.html
https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CDC reports at least 100 new measles cases in the United States between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31, according to the CDC's measles case counter: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html. The case count will be determined by subtracting the total number of cases reported as of 2025-12-02 from the total number of cases reported as of 2025-12-31.
subquestions.rationale: The number of new measles cases reported by the CDC between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31 is a relevant indicator of the trajectory of the measles outbreak in the United States. If the number of new cases is high, it may indicate that the outbreak is continuing to spread, which could increase the likelihood of at least 500 measles cases in 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: CDC reports at least 100 new measles cases in the US between 2025-12-02 and 2025-12-31. This means: (CDC total cases as of Dec 31) - (CDC total cases as of Dec 2) >= 100. Observable evidence: CDC weekly measles case tracker data showing cumulative totals at both endpoints.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'CDC measles cases United States December 2025' - to find case counts during the window; 2. 'CDC measles case count tracker 2025 total cases' - to find specific tallies near the start/end dates; 3. 'CDC measles 1798 1828 cases total November 25 December 2 2025' - to pin down Dec 2 starting count; 4. 'measles cases US 2012 2025 December weekly CDC update final count' - to find the end-of-window total.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate data points identified: (a) 1,828 cases as of ~Dec 2-3 (CIDRAP Dec 3 report: '30 additional cases during past week, bringing national total to 1,828'); (b) 1,912 cases as of Dec 9 (multiple sources citing CDC Dec 9 data); (c) 1,958 cases as of Dec 16 (CDC report per multiple sources); (d) 2,012 cases as of Dec 23 (multiple major sources: ABC News, CIDRAP, Gizmodo, The Hill); (e) 2,012 cases as of Dec 29 (CIDRAP Dec 29 article). No candidate events were rejected as all directly reference CDC data.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Starting count: ~1,828 cases as of December 2-3, 2025 ([CIDRAP Dec 3](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/us-measles-outbreak-tops-1800-cases-respiratory-illness-surveillance-returns)). End count: 2,012 cases as of December 23-29, 2025 ([CIDRAP Dec 29](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/us-measles-outbreak-tops-2000-known-infections), [ABC News Dec 30](https://abcnews.go.com/Health/us-measles-cases-surpass-2000-highest-30-years/story?id=128747603), [The Hill Dec 30](https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5666810-measles-outbreak-texas-2025/)). Calculation: 2,012 - 1,828 = 184 new cases during the window. This exceeds the 100-case threshold by 84 cases. Note: The CIDRAP Dec 3 article says this 1,828 was reached by adding 30 cases 'during the past week,' meaning the Dec 2 count was approximately 1,798. Either way, 2,012 - 1,798 = 214, or 2,012 - 1,828 = 184 — both well above 100.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Start timestamp: The CIDRAP article published 2025-12-03 reports 1,828 cases as of that weekly CDC update (covering data through approximately Dec 2). End timestamp: Multiple sources published 2025-12-29 and 2025-12-30 confirm 2,012 cases as of the CDC's most recent update (Dec 23, 2025). These timestamps are explicitly dated in published news sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks whether 100 new cases were added during the Dec 2-31 window total — not the first time a threshold was crossed. Based on weekly increments (~30-84 cases/week), the 100-case milestone within the window was reached approximately by early-to-mid December 2025: from ~1,828 (Dec 2) to 1,912 (Dec 9) represents ~84 new cases, and by Dec 16 (1,958) it would have crossed the 100-case mark (1,958 - 1,828 = 130). No earlier qualifying occurrence exists before Dec 2 for this window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: All sources consistently report rising case counts throughout December, with no contradictory reports suggesting a drop or data revision downward. The CDC weekly updates were consistent across multiple independent sources (CIDRAP, ABC News, The Hill, Gizmodo, NBC News). The question resolution depends on the difference between Dec 2 and Dec 31 counts. The Dec 31 count is not explicitly available (the last CDC update found is Dec 23 at 2,012), but: (a) cases continued rising through Dec 30 per South Carolina DPH reports and other state data; (b) the Dec 29 CIDRAP article still cites 2,012 as the CDC total, possibly reflecting a lag in CDC updates. Even using the most conservative interpretation (2,012 - 1,828 = 184), the threshold of 100 is far exceeded.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly and explicitly shows that the CDC reported approximately 1,828 cases around December 2, 2025, and 2,012 cases as of December 23-29, 2025. The difference (184 cases minimum, likely higher by Dec 31) substantially exceeds the 100-case threshold. Multiple high-quality sources confirm these figures. Resolution: Yes.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics release any employment data between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is responsible for releasing key economic data, including employment reports. However, the current government shutdown has suspended the release of these reports. According to the US Labor Department, the BLS will halt all scheduled economic data releases, including the September employment report, if the federal government shuts down (https://www.mint.com/news/today-news/us-labor-department-to-halt-economic-data-releases-if-government-shuts-down-1572358215515.html). https://www.mint.com/news/today-news/us-labor-department-to-halt-economic-data-releases-if-government-shuts-down-1572358215515.html 
https://www.afp.com/en/news/4156/us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-government-shutdown
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases any employment data between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31, as reported by the BLS official website (https://www.bls.gov/) or other credible sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/). The resolution source will check for any updates on the BLS release calendar (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release.htm) between the specified dates.
subquestions.rationale: The release of employment data by the BLS is a key indicator of the labor market conditions. If the BLS releases any employment data during the specified period, it could be an indicator that the shutdown is ending or that the BLS has found a way to release data despite the shutdown, which could in turn affect the release of the next jobs report.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: BLS releases any employment data between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31. 'Employment data' specifically refers to labor market indicators such as nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rates, weekly unemployment claims, and jobs reports — distinct from price/inflation data like CPI. Observable evidence would be any BLS press release, news report, or BLS website update confirming a release of employment/labor market data in this window. Key constraint: the government shutdown began October 1, 2025, halting most BLS operations.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Bureau of Labor Statistics employment data release October 2025' — to find any BLS employment data released in window. 2) 'BLS jobs report October 2025' — to find jobs report releases. 3) 'BLS CPI Consumer Price Index release October 24 2025' — to verify whether the CPI released on Oct 24 qualifies. 4) 'BLS employment data release October 2025 government shutdown' — to find context on what was or wasn't released. 5) 'BLS unemployment claims weekly data October 2025' — to check if weekly claims were released.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: BLS released September 2025 CPI on October 24, 2025 at 8:30 AM ET — CONFIRMED by multiple high-quality sources (Financial Express, UPI, BeInCrypto, Zero Hedge, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com). HOWEVER, CPI is inflation/price data, NOT employment data. Rejected as not matching 'employment data' criteria. Candidate event 2: BLS September jobs report (nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate) — CONFIRMED NOT RELEASED; multiple sources explicitly state this was delayed and skipped entirely (Workers World, Investopedia, Oregon Herald, Yahoo). Candidate event 3: Weekly unemployment claims — CONFIRMED NOT RELEASED; the October 14 InvestingChannel article explicitly states 'due to the ongoing government shutdown, the report will not be released.' Candidate event 4: State-level employment data — CONFIRMED NOT RELEASED; multiple state agencies confirmed BLS was not sharing underlying data. The BLS's own statement: 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires 'any employment data' from BLS. The only BLS data release in the window was the September CPI on October 24, 2025 [Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/investing-abroad-all-eyes-on-us-cpi-as-inflation-data-to-be-released-despite-government-shutdown-4020145/), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/10/24/Consumer-Price-Index/3261761306120/). CPI is inflation/price data, not employment data. Multiple sources confirm the September employment/jobs report was NOT released [Yahoo Oregon story](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/missing-federal-jobs-report-leaves-230723803.html), [Altoonamirror](https://www.altoonamirror.com/news/local-news/2025/10/govt-shutdown-pa-jobless-data-limbo/). Weekly unemployment claims were explicitly not released [InvestingChannel](https://news.investingchannel.com/article/700006/thursday-unemployment-claims-vehicle-sales-2). BLS explicitly stated: 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183). No employment data (jobs report, unemployment rate, nonfarm payrolls, weekly claims, state employment data) was released by BLS within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The ONLY BLS release in the window: September CPI released October 24, 2025 at 8:30 AM ET (13:30 UTC). This is price data, not employment data. For employment data: no timestamp can be established because no employment data was released. The Boston Globe (Oct 30) confirms 'the Bureau of Labor Statistics was able to release September inflation data because it was collected before the shutdown, but no new data has been gathered since' — confirming no employment data was released through October 30.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying employment data release occurred at all within the window, so the first occurrence check is moot. The government shutdown prevented all employment data releases from October 1 through at least October 31.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Could the CPI count as 'employment data'? BLS publishes both price statistics (CPI, PPI) and labor statistics (employment, wages). 'Employment data' is a specific category. The BLS's own structure separates 'Prices & Living Conditions' from 'Employment & Unemployment.' The resolution criteria refers to the 'BLS release calendar' which covers both. However, the question specifically says 'employment data,' not 'any BLS data.' The CPI is not employment data by any standard definition. Could any weekly unemployment claims have been released? Multiple sources confirm claims data was NOT released during the shutdown period (Anadolu Ajansı confirms BLS 'missed key reports, including...weekly unemployment claims'). The Boston Globe (Oct 30) confirms 'longest economic data blackout in history.' No contradictory evidence suggests any BLS employment data was released in the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS did NOT release any employment data between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31. The government shutdown (began October 1) halted all BLS employment data releases. The only BLS release in this window was the September CPI (inflation data) on October 24, 2025, which was a special exception for Social Security COLA calculations — and CPI is not 'employment data.' The jobs report, weekly unemployment claims, state employment data, and all other employment-related BLS publications were not released. This resolves No. The window closed on October 31 with no qualifying event occurring, so resolution_datetime = 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z.

evidence.step8_final_decision: A new insurrection trial (second martial law trial) began on September 26, 2025, as explicitly reported by Yonhap News Agency and KBS World Radio. question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members' public statements between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 indicate a majority support for a pause in interest rate changes at the December meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has been making decisions on interest rates, with recent cuts in September and October 2025. The current federal funds target range is 3.75%-4.00%. The FOMC's next meeting is scheduled for December 9-10, 2025. According to recent news articles, there are growing divisions within the FOMC, with some members supporting a pause in interest rate changes and others advocating for further cuts. For example, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell delivered a firm warning that a December interest-rate cut is not guaranteed, highlighting growing divisions within the FOMC (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powell-december-warning-exposes-hardening-140051111.html). Additionally, FOMC members such as Stephen Miran and Michelle Bowman have publicly expressed their views on interest rates, with Miran advocating for deeper cuts and Bowman warning that the labor market may already be deteriorating (https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbestreptalk/2025/10/04/fed-expected-to-cut-interest-rates-again-in-october/?sh=5a44466d66f2). Sources: 
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powell-december-warning-exposes-hardening-140051111.html 
https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbestreptalk/2025/10/04/fed-expected-to-cut-interest-rates-again-in-october/?sh=5a44466d66f2
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05, a majority of the FOMC members' public statements indicate support for a pause in interest rate changes at the December meeting, as reported by reputable news sources such as Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/) or CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/). The resolution will be based on the analysis of publicly available statements and articles from these sources.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides insight into the FOMC members' views on interest rates, which can influence the decision-making process at the December meeting. If a majority of FOMC members publicly support a pause in interest rate changes, it may indicate a higher likelihood of a pause at the December meeting, which is one of the conditions for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Between Nov 5-Dec 5, 2025, a majority (>50%) of FOMC members' public statements indicate support for a PAUSE (no rate change) at the December meeting. Observable evidence: Explicit statements by ≥7 of 12 FOMC voting members (or majority of total 19 members) favoring no rate change at December meeting, as reported by Bloomberg/CNBC or equivalent reputable sources. Key constraint: This must be measured across the entire window and must reflect a majority position.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'FOMC Federal Reserve members statements pause interest rate December 2025' — to find all member statements in window. 2. 'Federal Reserve interest rate hold December 2025 FOMC meeting' — to find hold/pause advocacy. 3. 'Federal Reserve officials majority support pause hold rates December 2025' — to find explicit majority characterizations. 4. 'Fed Powell Waller Williams Bowman December rate cut pause 2025 statement' — to identify specific member positions. 5. 'Fed rate cut December 2025 probability 80 90 percent market expectations' — to gauge overall sentiment at end of window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Early window (Nov 5-20): Multiple members supported pause — Collins, Schmid, Bostic, Musalem, Kashkari (non-voting), Hammack (non-voting). Cut supporters: Miran, Waller (from Nov 17), Bowman. Powell and Jefferson were neutral/cautious. Market odds fell to ~47% cut. Late window (Nov 21-Dec 5): Significant shift — Williams (Nov 21) explicitly supported cut, Waller (Nov 17), Bowman supported cuts. Collins said 'undecided' on Nov 23. Commerzbank analysis (Nov 24) said Board of Governors majority favored cut. Scotiabank projected 8-1-2 split for cut; Jefferies 7-5 slim cut majority. By Dec 4, market odds at 89.2% for cut. No single moment during the window showed an explicitly documented majority (>6 voting members) publicly supporting a pause.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires that 'a majority of the FOMC members' public statements indicate support for a pause.' Evidence shows: (1) In early November, several prominent members signaled pause-preference, but this was described as a divided/toss-up situation, not a clear majority for pause. Sources like [CNBC Nov 13](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/11/13/markets-rethink-december-rate-cut-amid-fed-doubts.html) and [Morningstar Nov 13](https://www.morningstar.com/markets/december-interest-rate-cut-is-now-coin-toss) described 50/50 odds, not a majority for pause. (2) By late November, the balance clearly shifted toward a majority supporting a CUT: [Commerzbank/FXStreet Nov 24](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/fomc-deeply-divided-over-timing-of-december-rate-cut-commerzbank-202511241144) said 'a majority within the seven-member Board of Governors appears to favor a December cut.' [Investopedia Nov 21](https://www.investopedia.com/december-rate-cut-seems-likelier-after-fed-officials-comments-11854375) showed odds rising to 73% cut. [Scotiabank analysis via Investing.com Nov 21](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-williams-revives-ratecut-hopes-but-would-a-split-fed-actually-cut-4373949) projected 8-1-2 split favoring cut. (3) By Dec 4-5, 89% market odds for cut; [BofA/Goldman/JPMorgan joined chorus expecting cut](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/bofa-joins-growing-chorus-expecting-fed-rate-cut-in-december/articleshow/125734868.cms). The evidence does NOT show a majority of FOMC members supporting a pause during the window — instead, the balance evolved toward majority supporting a cut.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The critical inflection point was Nov 21, 2025, when Williams' statement shifted market odds from ~39% to 73% for a cut. By Nov 24-25, market odds reached 79-85%. By Dec 4, odds were at 89.2%. No timestamp exists showing a majority of FOMC members explicitly and publicly supporting a pause (as opposed to the divided/uncertain stance described in early November).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence of a majority of FOMC members explicitly supporting a pause was found. The early November period showed roughly equal division or slight lean toward pause, but not an explicit majority. The later period showed a clear shift toward majority supporting a cut.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The October FOMC minutes (released Nov 20) said 'many participants expressed the view that maintaining the current benchmark rate for the remainder of the year would be appropriate' — this is the closest to a majority-for-pause signal, but: (a) it refers to October meeting participants' views at that time, not public statements in Nov 5-Dec 5 window, (b) 'many' is not explicitly 'majority', (c) subsequent public statements by Williams, Waller, Bowman, Miran shifted the balance. The Chosun.com Dec 4 article explicitly notes 'a significant number of regional Fed presidents advocate for a pause' — using 'significant number' rather than 'majority.' All analysis sources describe the December decision as divided or leaning toward a cut, never explicitly stating a majority favoring a pause during the Nov 5-Dec 5 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The evidence shows that while there was significant division among FOMC members throughout November 2025, a majority of FOMC members' public statements did NOT indicate support for a pause. In the early window (Nov 5-20), the situation was described as a 'toss-up' or 'coin flip,' not a clear majority for pause. By the end of the window (late November through Dec 5), multiple analyses from reputable sources (Commerzbank, Scotiabank, Jefferies, Goldman Sachs) indicated that the balance had shifted to a majority supporting a December cut, not a pause. Market odds rose to 89% for a cut by Dec 4. The resolution is definitively No, as a majority supporting a pause never emerged during the window — instead, the dominant trend by window close was majority-for-cut. Resolution datetime is set to 2025-12-05 as the window closed without the condition being met.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Key polls identified: (1) Victory Insights (Oct 22-23): Mamdani 47%, Cuomo 29% = lead of 18 pts. (2) Patriot Polling (Oct 18-19): Mamdani +11. (3) Suffolk University (Oct 23-26): Mamdani 44%, Cuomo 34% = lead of 10 pts. (4) Quinnipiac (Oct 23-27): Mamdani 43%, Cuomo 33% = lead of 10 pts. (5) Marist (Oct 24-28): Mamdani 48%, Cuomo 32% = lead of 16 pts. (6) Emerson/Pix11 (Oct 25-27): Mamdani 50%, Cuomo 25% = lead of 25 pts. (7) Fox News (Oct 2025): Mamdani 49%, Cuomo 28% = lead of 21 pts. (8) Marist (Oct 30, released): Mamdani 48%, Cuomo 32% = lead of 16 pts. (9) Fox News Poll (Oct 31): Mamdani 47%, Cuomo 31% = lead of 16 pts. (10) RealClearPolitics average (Oct 31): Mamdani 46.3%, Cuomo 30.7% = lead of ~15.6 pts.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The starting poll closest to Oct 23 was Victory Insights (Oct 22-23): Mamdani lead of 18 points [The News International](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1353588-zohran-mamdani-dominates-mayoral-contest-as-early-voting-begins-in-nyc). From 18 pts (Oct 23) to ~15-16 pts (Nov 1) = DECREASE, not increase. Even the highest late poll (Emerson: 25-pt lead) is cherry-picked against other polls showing narrowing. No individual poll shows a 5-pt increase in lead from a specific Oct 23 baseline to a Nov 1 reading.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Victory Insights poll (the benchmark poll at start of window) was conducted Oct 22-23 and published Oct 25, 2025. The Marist poll end of window was released Oct 30. The Fox News poll data point cited was published Oct 31, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event (a 5 pp lead increase) was found within the window. The polls consistently show a stable or slightly declining lead, not a 5-pt increase.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple polls from different organizations all published within the window were reviewed. End-of-window polls showed 10-16 points (most), with one outlier at 25 (Emerson). The overall trend showed either stability or slight decline, not a 5+ point increase. The Emerson poll (25-pt lead) vs. the start of 18 pts would represent an increase, but this is a different polling organization from the starting poll, making cross-pollster comparison unreliable for this resolution. RCP average went from ~18 pts (near Oct 23) to ~15.6 pts (Oct 31), a decrease. No poll showed a 5-pt lead increase using a consistent methodology.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The polling data shows Mamdani's lead did NOT increase by at least 5 percentage points between Oct 23 and Nov 1, 2025. Even the most favorable end-of-window poll (Emerson: 25 pts) represents a different polling organization than the starting point poll. The condition for Yes resolution (lead increasing by ≥5 pts) was definitively not met by Nov 1. Resolution: No.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The US Census Bureau/BEA released the advance goods trade estimate on September 25, 2025, showing the US goods trade deficit declined from $103.9 billion in July to $85.5 billion in August — a decline of approximately $18.4 billion, which exceeds the $10 billion threshold. question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a clean Continuing Resolution (CR) be proposed by either the House or the Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07?
subquestions.background_information:
The current government shutdown has led to a funding crisis, with Virginia community health centers facing a potential funding crisis as federal healthcare tax credits are set to expire, according to warnings from Sens. Mark Warner and Tim Kaine <https://www.wsls.com/news/virginia/2025/10/21/watch-virginia-community-health-centers-face-funding-crisis/>. The Senate has held multiple votes on a Republican-backed clean Continuing Resolution (CR), which would reopen and fund the government until mid-November, providing time to complete all 12 annual appropriations bills <https://www.starlocalmedia.com/news/no-progress-on-funding-as-trump-cuts-programs-amid-shutdown/article_2fbaeef4-55b4-11ec-9f3e-7b46f249d5a8.html>. A clean CR is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations. Sources: 
WSLS: https://www.wsls.com/ 
Star Local: https://www.starlocalmedia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a clean Continuing Resolution (CR) is proposed by either the House or the Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-07, as reported by credible news sources such as The New York Times <https://www.nytimes.com/> or Politico <https://www.politico.com/>. The proposal must be a formal introduction of a bill or resolution that meets the definition of a clean CR.
subquestions.rationale: The proposal of a clean CR by either the House or the Senate would be a significant indicator of the likelihood of a clean CR being passed, which is the ultimate question. If a clean CR is proposed, it would suggest that there is momentum and support for a clean CR, increasing the chances of it being passed.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: A clean Continuing Resolution (CR) — a government funding bill with no policy riders — must be formally introduced/proposed as a bill or resolution in either the House or Senate between October 31 and November 7, 2025. Observable evidence: A news report from a credible source explicitly stating that a clean CR was formally introduced in Congress within the window. Key entities: House, Senate, any member of Congress. Threshold: Must be 'clean' (no extraneous provisions) and must be a formal introduction of a bill or resolution.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'clean Continuing Resolution proposed House Senate November 2025' — to find any formal clean CR proposals. 2. 'Continuing Resolution CR bill introduced Congress November 2025' — to find formal introductions. 3. 'new clean CR introduced Senate November 2025 shutdown deal' — to find new CR proposals. 4. 'Senate Thune new continuing resolution bill introduced formal proposal shutdown' — to find specific formal filings. 5. 'Senate vote Friday clean CR shutdown November 7 2025' — to find the Nov 7 vote. 6. 'Senate shutdown deal Democrats clean CR proposal vote November 7' — to find the Schumer Nov 7 proposal.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) The existing House-passed clean CR from September 19, 2025, which was being voted on repeatedly in the Senate — this was passed BEFORE the question window and thus does not qualify. (2) Senate Majority Leader Thune's proposed new CR bundled with a minibus package — described as NOT a clean CR since it includes appropriations bills attached. (3) On November 7, 2025, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer unveiled a formal proposal that multiple sources describe as including a 'clean' continuing resolution along with three appropriations bills and ACA subsidies extension. This is the primary candidate event within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: On November 7, 2025, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer formally presented a proposal on the Senate floor. [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/democrats-new-offer-end-shutdown-republicans-reject-healthcare-rcna242643): 'Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer...introduced a new bipartisan proposal...featuring a 'clean' continuing resolution to reopen the government at current spending levels and a package of three appropriations bills...' [MSNBC](https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/news/democrats-shutdown-deal-republicans-torch-rcna242694): 'Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer...unveiled the first formal Democratic proposal to reopen the government. The plan included a 'clean' stopgap funding bill and three already-bipartisan-approved appropriations bills, along with a one-year extension of Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies...' However, the Schumer proposal is NOT purely a clean CR — it bundles the clean CR with ACA subsidies and appropriations bills. The clean CR is a component of a larger package, not a standalone clean CR. The resolution criteria specifies a 'formal introduction of a bill or resolution that meets the definition of a clean CR.' Schumer's proposal does not itself meet the definition of a clean CR; it contains a clean funding component within a larger non-clean package. This is a critical distinction. Furthermore, the existing Republican-backed CR (from September 19) was already in play during the window and was described as 'clean,' but it was introduced BEFORE the window opened.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Schumer's November 7 proposal: Multiple sources published on November 7, 2025 describe this as occurring on that date. However, no exact time within November 7 is specified. The date November 7, 2025 is within the resolution window (ending November 7, 2025 at 23:59:59).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Schumer proposal on November 7 appears to be the first formal Democratic proposal within the window. The existing House CR was proposed/passed on September 19, 2025 — before the window. No earlier clean CR introductions within the October 31 - November 7 window are found in the evidence.
evidence.step7_verification: Critical ambiguity: The resolution criteria requires a proposal that 'meets the definition of a clean CR.' Schumer's November 7 proposal is described as containing a clean CR component but is packaged with ACA subsidies extension — making the overall proposal NOT a clean CR. The individual clean funding element is part of a non-clean package. Multiple Republican sources explicitly rejected Schumer's proposal as not a clean CR (calling it a 'nonstarter' precisely because it included ACA policy demands). The existing House-passed clean CR (from September 19) continued to be voted on in the Senate during the window, but this represents votes on an already-proposed bill, not a new proposal within the window. There is no evidence of a standalone, purely clean CR being formally introduced as a new bill within the October 31 - November 7 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence does not conclusively establish that a standalone clean CR was formally introduced within the resolution window. The Schumer proposal on November 7 is the closest candidate, but it does not meet the strict definition of a 'clean CR' because it bundles a clean funding element with ACA subsidies extension and appropriations bills. While the NBC News and MSNBC articles do describe it as containing a 'clean' CR component, the overall proposal is not a clean CR. The resolution criteria requires the proposal itself to meet the definition of a clean CR. This ambiguity — whether a proposal that contains a clean CR element within a larger package counts — means the criteria cannot be definitively satisfied. The question is resolvable as No, since no standalone clean CR was formally introduced within the window, though the confidence level is moderated by the Schumer proposal's description as including a 'clean' stopgap. However, given that Schumer's proposal is explicitly NOT a clean CR in the traditional sense (it includes policy riders), resolution is No.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?

subquestions.question: Will the US court system rule in favor of Lisa Cook's lawsuit against Donald Trump's attempt to remove her from the Federal Reserve by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The current situation involves Donald Trump's attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged false statements in mortgage applications. Cook has denied wrongdoing and has begun legal action, stating that Trump has no authority to remove her. The Fed has reaffirmed its independence, stating it would abide by any court decision. According to an article by Yahoo! Finance, a federal judge will decide on August 30, 2025, whether to block President Donald Trump from removing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. The case is expected to reach the Supreme Court, where a conservative majority has previously allowed Trump to remove officials from other agencies, but a May order distinguished the Fed as a unique institution with a 'distinct historical tradition.' https://finance.yahoo.com/news/white-house-says-feds-cook-175151111.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the US court system rules in favor of Lisa Cook's lawsuit against Donald Trump's attempt to remove her from the Federal Reserve between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. The resolution source will be official court documents and reputable news sources, such as https://www.yahoo.com/ and https://www.cnn.com/. A ruling in favor of Cook would be defined as a court decision that prevents Trump from removing her from the Federal Reserve or a decision that declares Trump's attempt to remove her as unlawful.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it directly affects Trump's ability to influence the Federal Reserve. If the court rules in favor of Cook, it would limit Trump's power to remove Federal Reserve governors, making it less likely that he would try to fire another governor. On the other hand, if the court rules in favor of Trump, it would embolden him to take further action against the Federal Reserve, potentially leading to more attempts to remove governors.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: a US court ruling IN FAVOR of Lisa Cook's lawsuit between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, specifically defined as a court decision that either (a) prevents Trump from removing Cook from the Federal Reserve, OR (b) declares Trump's attempt to remove her as unlawful. Key entities: Lisa Cook, Donald Trump, Federal Reserve, US courts. Timing constraint: ruling must occur between Sept 1 and Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Lisa Cook lawsuit Trump Federal Reserve removal court ruling' (Sept–Oct 2025) — to find court decisions in window; 2) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve fired dismissed Trump 2025' (Jan–Oct 2025) — to find full timeline; 3) 'Lisa Cook court injunction preliminary ruling favor September 2025' — to find specific favorable rulings; 4) 'Lisa Cook Federal Reserve Supreme Court ruling September October 2025' — to find any Supreme Court action; 5) 'Supreme Court Lisa Cook Federal Reserve ruling October 1 2025' — to check exact SCOTUS timing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Sept 9/10, 2025: U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb issued preliminary injunction blocking Trump from removing Cook, explicitly stating Trump had not provided a legally permissible cause. (2) Sept 15/16, 2025: D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals (2-1) upheld the preliminary injunction and ruled Cook likely to prevail. (3) Oct 1, 2025: Supreme Court ruled Cook could stay pending Jan 2026 arguments — this is on the boundary date. All three were identified; events (1) and (2) clearly within the window; event (3) is dated October 1, exactly at the window's end date.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The preliminary injunction from Judge Jia Cobb on September 9/10, 2025 explicitly: (a) prevented Trump from removing Cook while litigation proceeds, and (b) stated 'President Trump has not stated a legally permissible cause for Cook's removal.' This directly satisfies BOTH prongs of the resolution criteria. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/lisa-cook-remain-us-central-073925944.html), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2025/09/10/federal-court-temporarily-blocks-trumps-firing-of-fed-governor-lisa-cook/), [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2025/09/court-issues-injunction-against-removal-of-cook-from-fed-board/), [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/sep/10/court-says-lisa-cook-stay-federal-reserve-board-governors-lawsuit/) all confirm the ruling on Sept 10, 2025. The D.C. Circuit also upheld this on Sept 15/16, 2025, per [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/appeals-court-blocks-trump-s-effort-to-immediately-remove-fed-governor-lisa-cook-11810690) and [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/09/15/appeals-court-lets-fed-governor-lisa-cook-stay-for-now/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources confirm the district court ruling was issued on September 9 or 10, 2025 (some sources report Sep 9, others Sep 10, likely reflecting that it was issued late Sep 9 and widely reported on Sep 10). The KSL article states 'ruling, issued on September 11 2025' but most other sources say Sept 9/10. The appeals court ruling was on September 15 or 16, 2025. Both are within the September 1 – October 1 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event was the district court preliminary injunction on September 9/10, 2025. There is no evidence of any qualifying court ruling in Cook's favor before September 9, 2025 (Trump only fired her on August 25, 2025, and she filed her lawsuit in late August). The September 9/10 injunction is confirmed as the first occurrence within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Trump administration appealed both rulings and then sought Supreme Court intervention, arguing Cook's removal was lawful. The Supreme Court on October 1 ruled Cook could remain 'for now' and agreed to hear arguments in January 2026 — this suggests the matter is not fully resolved. However, the resolution criteria only require a court ruling that 'prevents Trump from removing her' — not a final, permanent ruling. The preliminary injunction on September 9/10 clearly satisfies this criteria. The Trump administration's appeals do not negate the existence of court rulings in Cook's favor within the window. No contradictory evidence disproves the qualifying events occurred within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The US court system definitively ruled in favor of Lisa Cook within the September 1 – October 1, 2025 window. On September 9/10, 2025, U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb issued a preliminary injunction preventing Trump from removing Cook, explicitly finding he lacked 'legally permissible cause.' On September 15/16, 2025, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld that ruling 2-1. Both rulings satisfy the resolution criteria: they are court decisions that prevented Trump from removing Cook and/or declared his attempt unlawful. The first qualifying event occurred September 9/10, 2025. Resolution = Yes.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

subquestions.background_information:

The removal of the de minimis exemption has also affected Canadian exporters, who now face full duties and increased paperwork. According to the Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB), 46% of B.C. businesses expect to be impacted by the removal of the de minimis exemption [https://www.mycowichanvalleynow.com/2025/08/22/b-c-small-businesses-brace-for-end-of-u-s-duty-free-exemption/](https://www.mycowichanvalleynow.com/2025/08/22/b-c-small-businesses-brace-for-end-of-u-s-duty-free-exemption/). My Cowichan Valley Now [https://www.mycowichanvalleynow.com/](https://www.mycowichanvalleynow.com/)
NME Music News [https://www.nme.com/](https://www.nme.com/)
