The resolution source will also include reputable news outlets such as Bloomberg [https://www.bloomberg.com/](https://www.bloomberg.com/) or Reuters [https://www.reuters.com/](https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a change in tariff rates on Canadian goods could indicate a shift in the U.S. trade policy towards Canada, potentially leading to a reduction or removal of tariffs in the future.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: U.S. Customs and Border Protection announces a change to tariff rates on Canadian goods between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Observable evidence: Official CBP announcement or press release, or reporting by Bloomberg/Reuters confirming CBP has communicated a rate change. Key entities: CBP, Canadian goods, tariff rates. Timing: strictly within Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Customs Border Protection tariff rates Canadian goods announcement November 2025' - to find CBP-specific announcements. 2) 'CBP tariff change Canada November 2025' - targeting CBP actions. 3) 'US tariff increase Canada November 2025 CBP official announcement' - to verify if CBP issued new guidance. 4) 'Trump 10 percent tariff Canada October November 2025 implemented' - to check if the threatened tariff was implemented. 5) 'Section 232 tariff Canada USMCA November 2025 vehicles buses' - to check for new Section 232 tariffs affecting Canada.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Section 232 tariffs on medium/heavy-duty vehicles (25%) and buses (10%) took effect November 1, 2025, affecting Canadian goods with USMCA-partial relief; reported by multiple sources including Japan Times, JD Supra, Macau Business, ConnectGujarat. (2) Trump's threatened additional 10% tariff on Canada (announced Oct 25, 2025) - REJECTED: Multiple explicit sources from November 23-24, 2025 (E&E News, Politico via Korean outlet) confirm 'CBP has not received instructions to raise tariffs' and 'importers have not received any new regulatory guidance' as of November 24, 2025. (3) De minimis rule removal (November 26, 2025) - affects all international sellers including Canadians shipping to U.S., but this is not a Canada-specific tariff rate change.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Section 232 tariffs effective November 1, 2025 represent a change to tariff rates on goods from Canada (Canada accounts for ~20% of U.S. heavy truck imports per [connectgujarat.com](https://connectgujarat.com/world/us-tariffs-on-heavy-trucks-buses-come-into-effect-10612646)). The JD Supra November 2025 Customs and Trade newsletter [jdsupra.com](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/as-the-customs-and-trade-world-turns-3960617/) confirms 'Section 232 tariffs took effect on November 1 for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (MHDVs) and parts (25% duty) and buses (10% duty), with USMCA relief... and potential steel/aluminum tariff relief for Canadian and Mexican suppliers.' These tariffs apply to Canadian goods entering the U.S. and were enforced by CBP. The threatened Canada-specific 10% tariff was explicitly NOT implemented per [E&E News](https://www.eenews.net/articles/a-month-later-trump-has-yet-to-follow-through-on-canada-tariff-threat/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Section 232 tariffs on MHDV/buses took effect on 2025-11-01 (November 1, 2025), which falls within the resolution window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30). Multiple sources explicitly state this effective date.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying event within the window is the Section 232 tariff implementation on November 1, 2025. No earlier qualifying event exists within the window (the window starts October 31, 2025, and no tariff change is reported for that date specifically).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Trump-threatened 10% Canada-specific tariff was NOT implemented as confirmed by E&E News (Nov 24) and Politico (Nov 23). However, the Section 232 tariffs on vehicles/buses DID take effect November 1 and do affect Canadian goods. The resolution criteria asks about 'tariff rates on Canadian goods' — the Section 232 tariff is not Canada-specific but applies to all imports including Canadian goods. The question asks whether CBP 'announced a change to the tariff rates on Canadian goods' — the November 1 Section 232 tariff change was a CBP-enforced tariff change affecting Canadian goods, reported by reputable sources. The criteria does not require a Canada-exclusive announcement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Section 232 tariffs on medium/heavy-duty vehicles (25%) and buses (10%) took effect on November 1, 2025, within the resolution window. These tariffs apply to Canadian goods (with partial USMCA relief), representing a change to tariff rates on Canadian goods enforced by CBP. This event is explicitly reported by multiple reputable news outlets within the window. However, there is ambiguity: the question specifically frames it as CBP announcing a change 'on Canadian goods,' which could be interpreted as requiring a Canada-specific announcement (which would not resolve Yes, since the threatened 10% Canada-specific tariff was never implemented). The Section 232 tariff is a broader change affecting many countries but including Canada. Given this interpretive ambiguity, and that the question explicitly references CBP's official website and press releases — which the Section 232 implementation was broadly covered through — I find sufficient evidence that a tariff rate change affecting Canadian goods was announced and implemented by CBP within the window on November 1, 2025. The resolution is Yes.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report a seasonally adjusted decrease in nonfarm payroll employment of at least 50,000 jobs between the November 2025 and December 2025 reports?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. labor market has been experiencing downward revisions in employment data, with the BLS revising its estimate of nonfarm payroll growth for the year ending March 2025 down by 911,000 jobs <https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/bls-revises-job-growth-march-165530456.html>. This revision signals a weaker labor market, with slower hiring and stagnating wage growth. The BLS has also canceled the October 2025 report due to incomplete household data collection, and the November 2025 report has been rescheduled to December 16, 2025 <https://talkmarkets.com/member/ArcaMax/article/us-payrolls-marked-down-a-record-911000-in-preliminary-estimate?post=384438>. The Federal Reserve's next FOMC meeting is on December 10, 2025, and the delay in employment data increases the likelihood of a pause in rate cuts. Sources: 
https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/bls-revises-job-growth-march-165530456.html 
https://talkmarkets.com/member/ArcaMax/article/us-payrolls-marked-down-a-record-911000-in-preliminary-estimate?post=384438
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the BLS reports a seasonally adjusted decrease in nonfarm payroll employment of at least 50,000 jobs between the November 2025 and December 2025 reports, as reported on the BLS website <https://www.bls.gov/> or the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) website <https://fred.stlouisfed.org/>. The resolution window is between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides an early indicator of the labor market's performance in the last quarter of 2025. A decrease in nonfarm payroll employment of at least 50,000 jobs would suggest a weakening labor market, which could be a precursor to larger job cuts in 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question asks whether BLS reported a seasonally adjusted decrease in nonfarm payroll employment of at least 50,000 jobs between the November 2025 and December 2025 reports, within the window 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30. Key thresholds: ≥50,000 decrease, seasonally adjusted nonfarm payroll, comparison between two specific monthly BLS reports.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BLS nonfarm payroll employment December 2025 report jobs' (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30) — to find the December 2025 report data. Query 2: 'Bureau of Labor Statistics jobs report December 2025 November employment' (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30) — to find December report details. Query 3: 'BLS employment situation November 2025 report October jobs' (2025-10-01 to 2025-11-30) — to find what the November 2025 report contained. Query 4: 'BLS December 2025 jobs report November payroll level' (2025-12-15 to 2025-12-30) — to find specific level comparisons.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key facts established: (1) Due to 43-day government shutdown (Oct 1–Nov 12, 2025), the 'November 2025 report' was the delayed September employment report, released November 20, 2025, showing +119,000 September jobs. (2) The 'December 2025 report' was a combined October+November report released December 16, 2025, showing October: −105,000 and November: +64,000, plus downward revisions of −33,000 to August and September. (3) October nonfarm payrolls fell by 105,000—exceeding the 50,000 threshold for a single month. (4) Net change from September level to November level: −105K+64K = −41K (below threshold); including revisions: −41K−33K = −74K (above threshold).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires a 'decrease in nonfarm payroll employment of at least 50,000 jobs between the November 2025 and December 2025 reports.' Multiple interpretations exist: (a) If interpreted as the net change in the payroll level from the last data point in the November report (September) to the last data point in the December report (November): net = −41,000, which is BELOW the 50,000 threshold. (b) If revisions to August and September (−33,000 total) are included: net = −74,000, ABOVE threshold. (c) If the October monthly figure (−105,000) is used as 'the' change reported in the December report: ABOVE threshold. Multiple sources confirm the figures: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/16/jobs-report-november-2025-.html), [Yahoo Finance](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/us-job-growth-beats-expectations-133824526.html), [CalculatedRisk](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/12/november-employment-report-64-thousand.html).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The December 2025 BLS report was released on 2025-12-16, within the resolution window. The November 2025 BLS report was released on 2025-11-20, before the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The December 2025 report was the first and only BLS report released within the resolution window (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-30). It was released on December 16, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: The resolution criteria is ambiguous. The question was written assuming a normal monthly BLS release schedule (November report covering October data, December report covering November data). Due to the unprecedented government shutdown, the schedule was disrupted: the November 2025 report actually reported September data, and the December report was a combined October+November report. The net payroll change depends on interpretation: purely September→November = −41K (below threshold); September→November plus revisions = −74K (above threshold); or just October month = −105K (above threshold). This ambiguity prevents definitive resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria cannot be definitively applied because: (1) The unprecedented government shutdown created an unusual reporting situation not anticipated by the question's design; (2) The 'November 2025 report' reported September data (not October), making the 'between reports' comparison non-standard; (3) The net change from the November report's last data point to the December report's last data point is approximately −41,000 (below threshold) without revisions, or −74,000 (above threshold) with revisions; (4) The October monthly decline of −105,000 exceeds the threshold but was not the standalone 'December report' figure. The question is resolvable=false due to interpretive ambiguity.

Query 4: 'India Pakistan ceasefire violation Line of Control number increase 2025 report' - to find comparative data. Query 5: 'LoC India Pakistan Jammu Kashmir cross border firing violation 300 2025' - to find aggregate statistics.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) October 28 LoC violation in Lipa Valley (India.com, not India Today or NDTV); (2) October 13-14 firing/infiltration in Kupwara Machil/Dudniyal sectors (India Today, but classified as infiltration attempt, not ceasefire violation count data); (3) September 20 small-arms exchange in Nowgam sector (Army explicitly stated it did NOT constitute a ceasefire violation); (4) News18 article referenced '300 violations in 2025' as annual total - not a period-specific count. All rejected because: no source provides numerical count data for the specific 30-day windows required, no India Today or NDTV provides comparative statistics, and most LoC-related events during the period were either not confirmed as official ceasefire violations or lacked count data.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article from India Today [indiatoday.in] or NDTV [ndtv.com] was found providing: (a) a specific count of ceasefire violations for the period 2025-10-15 to 2025-11-14, (b) a specific count for the previous period 2025-09-15 to 2025-10-14, or (c) a comparative analysis showing a percentage change. The India Today article from Oct 13 [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/loc-tension-kupwara-firing-blasts-infiltration-machil-dudniyal-2802647-2025-10-14] reports an incident but provides no count data. No NDTV article was found covering India-Pakistan LoC violations in this context. The resolution criteria explicitly require data from these two sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for the required event because the required data (numerical counts from India Today and NDTV showing a ≥20% increase) was not published or found in any available sources during the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The Indian Army explicitly denied ceasefire violations on multiple occasions (August 2025, September 20 2025 exchange), suggesting the LoC was relatively calm post-Operation Sindoor ceasefire. The dominant theme in the Oct 15 - Nov 14 window was Pakistan-Afghanistan border violations, not India-Pakistan LoC violations. The only confirmed India-Pakistan LoC violation within the window was October 28 in Lipa Valley, but no aggregate count comparison data exists. Alternative interpretation: Even if violations occurred, without the specific numerical comparative data from India Today/NDTV that the resolution criteria require, the question cannot be resolved Yes.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question cannot be resolved because: (1) No numerical count data for India-Pakistan LoC ceasefire violations exists for either the measurement period (2025-10-15 to 2025-11-14) or the baseline period (2025-09-15 to 2025-10-14) from India Today or NDTV; (2) The resolution criteria specifically require data from these two named sources; (3) The underlying data required for comparison is missing and unavailable; (4) No article provides the comparative percentage analysis needed. evidence.step3_event_detection: TURKEY (NATO member): (1) Dec 15, 2025 – drone shot down by Turkish F-16s after entering Turkish airspace from the Black Sea, approaching Elmadağ/Çankırı area (deep inside Turkey). Sources: AP, The Straits Times, Euronews, C4ISRNET, multiple others. Note: origin unconfirmed by Turkey. (3) ~Dec 19, 2025 – Russian-made Orlan-10 drone found crashed in Kocaeli province (~50km from Istanbul). Sources: Times of India, AFP, Asharq Al-Awsat, Charter97. Origin unconfirmed officially but Turkey warned Russia/Ukraine, suggesting Russian/Ukrainian origin [AP](https://apnews.com/article/drone-f16-black-sea-turkey-ukraine-russia-4a5880f62aa2c2c28cc32231a96234f2), [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/turkey-says-it-downs-uncontrolled-drone-over-black-sea). (3) ~Dec 19 – Russian Orlan-10 found crashed in Kocaeli. Drone physically entered and crashed in Turkish territory, initial Turkish Interior Ministry assessment identified it as Russian-made [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/88Q96G6), [Asharq Al-Awsat](https://english.aawsat.com/node/5221183). All within the 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks for AT LEAST 5 incidents, not a first occurrence threshold. The first qualifying incident appears to be December 10, 2025 (Merlin-VR found in Balıkesir, disclosed Dec 21), or December 15, 2025 (drone shot down over Turkey). All five incidents identified fall within the Nov 30 – Dec 29 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Turkey officially called the Dec 15 drone 'unidentified' and did not publicly confirm Russian origin, though it warned Russia/Ukraine. Some sources (Euromaidan Press) claim it was Russian; AP and Straits Times report the incident without attributing to Russia specifically. The Army Technology article noted ~20 incidents of Russian violations of European airspace in October 2025 alone, with high frequency continuing. Multiple credible sources (AP, Straits Times, AFP, Euronews) confirm Turkish drone incidents within the window. Even with conservative counting (requiring explicit 'Russian' attribution), there are 3-5 clear incidents in Turkey involving Russian-made/Russian-origin drones that crashed or were shot down within Turkish territory. The weight of evidence strongly supports that at least 5 Russian drone breaches of NATO airspace occurred in this period.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence supports resolution as YES. Within the Nov 30–Dec 29, 2025 window, at least 5 incidents of Russian drones breaching NATO member airspace (specifically Turkey, a NATO member) are reported by credible sources: (1) Dec 10 – Russian Merlin-VR drone crashed in Balıkesir, Turkey; (2) Dec 15 – unidentified drone (later suspected Russian) shot down inside Turkish airspace; (3) Dec 19 – Russian Orlan-10 drone found crashed in Kocaeli, Turkey; (4) Dec 20 – suspected Russian drone found crashed near Manyas/Balıkesir, Turkey; (5) Dec 25 – drone described as Russian shot down over Turkish airspace. question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the daily growth rate of the U.S. national debt exceed $10 billion per day between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt has been increasing rapidly, with the debt surpassing $37 trillion in August 2025, according to the Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimates that the debt will continue to grow, with a projected increase of $1.8 trillion in fiscal year 2025 (https://www.cbo.gov/publication/57411). The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget warns that if the current fiscal trajectory continues, the national debt could exceed $53 trillion by 2035 (https://www.crfb.org/papers/2025-fiscal-outlook). Sources: 
Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget: https://www.crfb.org/ 
Congressional Budget Office: https://www.cbo.gov/ 
Treasury Department: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the daily growth rate of the U.S. national debt exceeds $10 billion per day between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19, as reported by the Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). The daily growth rate will be calculated by taking the difference in debt values between two consecutive days and dividing by the number of days. If the Treasury Department's website becomes unavailable, alternative sources such as the Congressional Budget Office (https://www.cbo.gov/) or the Federal Reserve Economic Data (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/) will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The daily growth rate of the U.S. national debt is an indicator of the country's fiscal health and can provide insight into whether the debt will reach $38 trillion by the end of 2025. A high daily growth rate could suggest that the debt is increasing rapidly and may reach $38 trillion sooner rather than later.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The daily growth rate of U.S. national debt (day-over-day consecutive difference from Treasury 'Debt to the Penny') must exceed $10 billion on at least one day between Oct 1–Oct 19, 2025. Key threshold: >$10B single-day change. Key entity: U.S. Treasury gross national debt. Timing: Oct 1–Oct 19, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. national debt daily growth rate October 2025' — to find reported daily growth metrics during the window. 2) 'US national debt total October 2025 Treasury' — to find absolute debt values on specific dates. 3) 'US national debt $38 trillion crossed surpassed October 2025' — to pinpoint when $38T was crossed. 4) 'national debt increase $10 billion single day October 2025' — to find any explicit reporting of a $10B+ single-day spike. 5) 'Treasury debt to the penny daily October 16-19 2025' — to find daily granular data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources report the average daily growth rate during October 2025 as approximately $5.96–6 billion per day (based on annual $2.17 trillion increase ÷ 365 days). No source explicitly reports a single day exceeding $10 billion during Oct 1–19. The debt was ~$37.85T on Oct 3, ~$37.86T on Oct 8, ~$37.9T on Oct 10, and ~$37.8T on Oct 15, reaching $38.019T on Oct 21. The total increase from ~Oct 1 ($37.85T estimated) to Oct 21 ($38.019T) was approximately $170B over ~20 days ≈ $8.5B/day average. ZeroHedge noted 'delayed spending moving into October' could create spikes, but no source provides day-by-day Treasury figures confirming any single day >$10B within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require day-over-day difference exceeding $10B. Multiple authoritative sources consistently report the average daily growth at ~$6B/day. The JEC Senate report [jec.senate.gov] explicitly states '$5.96 billion per day' as of Oct 3. The Yahoo Finance/Cryptopolitan sources report ~$6B/day. No source provides Treasury daily data (Debt to the Penny) showing a single-day change >$10B within the window. The total increase across the window (~$170B over 20 days) suggests an average below $10B/day. No event is explicitly reported meeting the $10B single-day threshold within Oct 1–19.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a $10B+ single-day event within the window because no such event is explicitly reported. The $38T milestone was crossed on Oct 21, 2025 — outside the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checking: The debt went from ~$37.85T (early October) to $38.019T (Oct 21) — approximately $169B over ~18–20 days, averaging $8.4–9.4B/day at the upper bound. Even at the upper bound of estimated total increase, the average remains below $10B/day. The consistent reporting across JEC, Cryptopolitan, Yahoo Finance, and other sources all cite ~$6B/day. No contradictory evidence showing a single day >$10B was found. The government shutdown (started Oct 1) and delayed spending from September could cause some daily volatility, but no specific day is reported as exceeding $10B. Resolution requires explicit evidence, not inference.
evidence.step8_final_decision: All available evidence indicates the daily growth rate of U.S. national debt consistently ran at approximately $5.96–6 billion per day during the Oct 1–19, 2025 window. The $38 trillion milestone was crossed on October 21, 2025, just outside the window, further supporting that growth was below $10B/day on average throughout the window. No source explicitly reports any single day within Oct 1–19 exceeding $10B/day. The condition is not met. Resolution: No.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the building located at 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E in Bilytske, Donetsk Oblast, by the specified date ET.

The building will be considered captured if any part of the building is shaded red under a below-specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the building under the above-specified conditions, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Building Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP1.png

Building Location in Bilytske: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP2.png

Bilytske Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP3.png

Location on Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/J8DsAv3gKWbD4DSD9

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap is rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces advance by at least 5 square kilometers in the Donetsk region between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14, according to the DeepStateMap?
subquestions.background_information: The current conflict in Ukraine has seen Russian forces making gradual advances in the Donetsk region. According to the Institute for the Study of War, Russian forces have captured around 76.7% of the Donetsk region as of August 2025 <https://www.understandingwar.org/>. The Ukrainian General Staff has reported that Russia currently holds approximately 19% of Ukrainian territory <https://www.thestraitstimes.com/>. The DeepStateMap is a reliable source for tracking changes in control on the ground <https://deepstatemap.live/>.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Russian forces advance by at least 5 square kilometers in the Donetsk region between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14, according to the DeepStateMap https://deepstatemap.live/. The advance must be reflected in the map updates during this period. If the DeepStateMap is unavailable, the ISW Ukraine map https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 may be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: The question is relevant to the ultimate question because an advance by Russian forces in the Donetsk region could indicate increased momentum and pressure on Ukrainian forces, potentially leading to the capture of Bilytske. The DeepStateMap is a reliable source for tracking changes in control on the ground, and an advance of at least 5 square kilometers would be a significant indicator of Russian progress.
Sources: Institute for the Study of War: https://www.understandingwar.org/

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Russian forces must advance by at least 5 square kilometers in the Donetsk region between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14, as reflected in DeepStateMap updates. Observable evidence: DeepStateMap (or ISW fallback) showing territorial gains ≥5 sq km in Donetsk. Key entities: Russian forces, Donetsk Oblast, DeepStateMap. Threshold: 5 sq km minimum. Timing: strictly within 2026-01-15 to 2026-02-14.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russian forces advance Donetsk territory January February 2026' — to find overall advance data; 2) 'DeepStateMap Ukraine territory control Donetsk 2026' — to find DeepState-specific data; 3) 'Russian territory gains square kilometers Donetsk January 2026 ISW' — to find ISW/quantified data; 4) 'DeepState map Russia advance Donetsk square kilometers February 2026' — to find DeepState sq km data; 5) 'DeepState January 2026 Donetsk Oblast 59 km advance Seversk Konstantinovka' — to confirm specific DeepState data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Charter97/DeepState data showing 59.6 km² gained between Seversk-Konstantinovka and 37.6 km² near Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast (January 2026); (2) Multiple DeepState-specific advances in Donetsk Oblast reported on Jan 19, 20, 26, 29, Feb 4, 5, 9, 10, 12 — all within the window; (3) AFP/ISW data showing 481 sq km gained across Ukraine in January 2026, with ~83% of Donetsk under Russian control. No events were rejected — all clearly satisfy criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Charter97 article (Jan 26, 2026) explicitly cites DeepState project data showing Russian forces gained 59.6 km² between Seversk and Konstantinovka in Donetsk Oblast and 37.6 km² near Pokrovsk — totaling ~97+ km² in Donetsk Oblast in January 2026 alone. [Charter97](https://charter97.org/en/news/2026/1/26/671362/) This vastly exceeds the 5 km² threshold. Additionally, Ukrainska Pravda reports multiple DeepState-confirmed advances in Donetsk Oblast throughout the window: [Jan 19](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/01/19/8016840/), [Jan 26](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/01/26/8017873/), [Jan 29](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/01/29/8018463/), [Feb 5](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/02/05/8019622/), [Feb 9](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/02/09/8020095/), [Feb 10](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/02/10/8020414/), [Feb 12](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/02/13/8020804/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest qualifying event within the resolution window: DeepState reported advances near Pokrovsk (Donetsk Oblast) on January 19, 2026 (article published 2026-01-19 by Ukrainska Pravda). The Charter97 article (published 2026-01-26) explicitly quantifies gains in Donetsk Oblast at 59.6 km² (Seversk-Konstantinovka) and 37.6 km² (Pokrovsk) in January 2026, citing DeepState. These advances began from January 1, 2026, but were clearly ongoing and being reported within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The resolution window starts 2026-01-15. The first qualifying DeepState-confirmed advance in Donetsk Oblast within the window appears to be January 19, 2026 (advance near Siversk, Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk per DeepState). The cumulative DeepState data showing >5 sq km advance in Donetsk was almost certainly met within the first few days of the resolution window given the scale of advances reported (~97+ km² for all of January, with Donetsk being the primary theater). No earlier qualifying occurrence outside the window would disqualify this.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The February 6, 2026 DeepState report notes 78% of Donetsk Oblast is under Russian control (up from previous levels), confirming advances. The February 12 Straits Times article notes DeepState as source for tracking territorial gains. NATO Secretary General Rutte's comment on Feb 13 about slow Russian advance refers to overall minimal gains vs losses but does not contradict Donetsk-specific gains of 5+ km². The Charter97 article headline 'pace almost tripled' refers to a tripling vs earlier period, but the December figure of 423 km² shows that even in 'slow' periods, gains far exceeded 5 km². No evidence of a ceasefire that would have stopped advances during the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly confirms that Russian forces advanced by far more than 5 square kilometers in the Donetsk region between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14, as recorded by DeepStateMap. DeepState data explicitly shows ~59.6 km² gained between Seversk-Konstantinovka and ~37.6 km² near Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast during January 2026. Multiple DeepState-reported advances throughout the resolution window confirm continuous territorial gains. The 5 km² threshold was met very early in the resolution window (likely within the first days). Resolution: Yes.

question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a bill or executive action be introduced in the US Congress or by the Trump administration to establish a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions between $200 and $600 before December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: There have been recent efforts by lawmakers and industry leaders to push for a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions. For example, Senator Cynthia Lummis has proposed a bill to exempt small Bitcoin transactions from capital gains taxes, and Jack Dorsey has urged lawmakers to adopt a de minimis tax exemption for everyday Bitcoin transactions <https://cryptonews.com/news/senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorsey-push-bitcoin-tax-exemption-2025-10-09.htm>. Additionally, a coalition of over 70 cryptocurrency and blockchain organizations has sent a letter to President Donald Trump urging immediate regulatory clarity for digital assets, including the application of de minimis tax rules <https://coincentral.com/crypto-christmas-wish-white-house-act-now-regulatory-clarity/>. The current IRS rules treat cryptocurrencies as property, triggering taxable events for every transaction, regardless of size, which can hinder Bitcoin's use as a medium of exchange <https://decrypt.co/83141/dorsey-lummis-push-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-expands-btc-payments>.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a bill or executive action is introduced in the US Congress or by the Trump administration to establish a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions between $200 and $600 between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. The resolution will be based on official information from the US federal government, including the Congressional Record <https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record> and the Federal Register <https://www.federalregister.gov/>. Additionally, credible reporting from reputable sources such as CoinDesk <https://www.coindesk.com/> and Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/> will be used to confirm the introduction of such a bill or executive action.
subquestions.rationale: The introduction of a bill or executive action to establish a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions would be a significant step towards reducing the regulatory burden on the industry and could increase the likelihood of Trump enacting a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026. This subquestion provides an early indicator of the progress towards the ultimate question and can help forecasters update their predictions.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: A bill or executive action introduced in US Congress or by Trump administration establishing a de minimis tax exemption specifically for cryptocurrency transactions between $200 and $600. Time window: 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29. Key entities: US Congress, Trump administration. Threshold: exemption range of $200-$600 (not under $200 or above $600). Must be formally 'introduced' per resolution criteria.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'cryptocurrency de minimis tax exemption bill Congress 2025' (to find any crypto tax bills in the window). Query 2: 'crypto de minimis tax exemption $200 $600 legislation' (to find bills matching the specific threshold). Query 3: 'Virtual Currency Tax Fairness Act de minimis crypto $200 $600 2025' (to find the specific threshold range). Query 4: 'Trump executive order cryptocurrency tax exemption de minimis 2025' (to check for executive actions). Query 5: 'PARITY Act Digital Asset $200 $600 de minimis cryptocurrency threshold range' (to verify PARITY Act threshold).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Primary candidate event: Digital Asset PARITY Act introduced as discussion draft on December 20, 2025 by Reps. Max Miller and Steven Horsford. This bill includes a de minimis exemption for stablecoin transactions. However: (1) The threshold is UNDER $200, not between $200 and $600. (2) The bill is a 'discussion draft' and 'not yet formally introduced as legislation.' (3) The exemption applies only to stablecoins, not all cryptocurrency. No other bills or executive actions matching the $200-$600 range were found. Senator Lummis' bill from July 2025 proposed a $300 threshold but was introduced before the window (July 2025), and was not re-introduced in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The PARITY Act does NOT match the resolution criteria: (1) The threshold mismatch is critical — the PARITY Act exempts transactions UNDER $200, while the criteria require an exemption for transactions BETWEEN $200 AND $600. These are fundamentally different threshold structures. (2) Multiple sources confirm the exemption is for amounts under $200: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-introduces-bill-fix-tax-163555254.html), [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/new-us-crypto-tax-law-parity-act-proposal/), [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/12/22/u-s-bipartisan-lawmakers-draw-up-tax-bill-with-stablecoin-and-staking-relief), [Brave New Coin](https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/us-lawmakers-propose-tax-breaks-for-small-stablecoin-payments-and-staking-rewards). (3) The bill is a 'discussion draft' not yet formally introduced per [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/12/22/u-s-bipartisan-lawmakers-draw-up-tax-bill-with-stablecoin-and-staking-relief) and [TechStory](https://techstory.in/house-lawmakers-unveil-bipartisan-parity-act-to-overhaul-crypto-taxes/). No executive action matching the criteria was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The PARITY Act discussion draft was circulated on December 20, 2025 (within the window), but it does not match the criteria for multiple reasons (wrong threshold, discussion draft only, stablecoins only). No other qualifying event found with a valid timestamp.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window exists. The PARITY Act (under $200, stablecoins only, discussion draft) is the only candidate, and it doesn't satisfy the $200-$600 range requirement.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources confirm the PARITY Act threshold is UNDER $200, not between $200-$600. CoinDesk (a named source in the resolution criteria) explicitly confirms the exemption is for 'low-value stablecoin transactions under $200.' No evidence found of any bill or executive action proposing a $200-$600 de minimis range for cryptocurrency transactions within the window. The resolution criteria's specific threshold of '$200 and $600' is not met by any identified legislation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition was NOT met within the window. The only relevant bill introduced during the window (PARITY Act discussion draft, December 20, 2025) proposes a de minimis exemption under $200 for stablecoins only, which does not match the required threshold of 'between $200 and $600' for cryptocurrency transactions generally. Additionally, the PARITY Act is only a discussion draft, not formally introduced legislation. No executive action matching the criteria was found. Resolution: No.

question: Will Atlas introduce ads by December 31?
description:

Limited advertisement releases restricted to a specific region, version, or user group will qualify. The release must be publicly announced as accessible to the relevant users. Closed betas or fully private testing do not count.

Once implemented, the market will resolve to “Yes” immediately, regardless of whether the integration is later removed.

An announcement will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes"; only the release of the specified advertisement integration will trigger a "Yes" resolution for this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI announce a partnership with at least one major advertising company between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23?
subquestions.background_information: OpenAI has recently launched its AI-powered web browser, ChatGPT Atlas, which integrates ChatGPT directly into the browsing experience. This move is seen as a potential precursor to OpenAI entering the advertising market, competing with Google's search ad business. According to Gil Luria, an analyst at D.A. Davidson, integrating chat into a browser could be a strategic step toward monetizing services through advertising <https://www.greekreporter.com/2025/10/23/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas-to-rival-google-chrome/>. OpenAI's CEO, Sam Altman, has also announced that ChatGPT now has 800 million weekly active users, up from 400 million in February 2025 <https://www.nairametrics.com/2025/10/openai-launches-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-powered-web-browser-to-rival-google/>.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if OpenAI announces a partnership with at least one major advertising company between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23. The resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI, as well as credible news outlets such as TechCrunch <https://techcrunch.com/> and The Verge <https://www.theverge.com/>.
subquestions.rationale: A partnership with a major advertising company would be a significant indicator of OpenAI's intentions to enter the advertising market, which could potentially lead to the introduction of ads in Atlas. This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides insight into OpenAI's business strategy and potential revenue streams.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: OpenAI announces a formal partnership with at least one major advertising company (e.g., WPP, Publicis, Omnicom, IPG, Dentsu, Google Ads, Meta, etc.) between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23. Observable evidence: Official announcement from OpenAI or major advertising company, confirmed by TechCrunch, The Verge, or similar outlets. Key threshold: 'major advertising company' excludes small SMB marketing agencies.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'OpenAI partnership advertising company 2025' [general search]; (2) 'OpenAI advertising deal announcement' [specific deals]; (3) 'OpenAI advertising agency WPP GroupM Publicis IPG' [major agency names]; (4) 'OpenAI ads business advertising revenue deal announcement November 2025'; (5) 'OpenAI SearchKings advertising partnership'; (6) 'OpenAI PayPal commerce partnership'; (7) 'Omnicom OpenAI partnership advertising'; (8) 'OpenAI advertising company WPP Publicis Omnicom IPG Dentsu'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) OpenAI-SearchKings partnership (Nov 13, 2025) - SearchKings is a small/medium SMB-focused digital marketing agency, NOT a major advertising company; (2) OpenAI-PayPal partnership (Oct 28, 2025) - PayPal is a payments company, not an advertising company; (3) Omnicom winning OpenAI as a client (mentioned in marketing-interactive.com article) - this is Omnicom providing advertising services TO OpenAI, not a partnership between OpenAI and Omnicom in the advertising space; (4) OpenAI exploring ads internally - articles from Nov 17-18 discuss hints about ChatGPT ads but no formal advertising partnership was announced. All candidates rejected as not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event explicitly satisfies 'OpenAI announces a partnership with at least one major advertising company.' The SearchKings partnership [prnewswire.com, Nov 13] involves a small SMB-focused agency, not a major advertising company. The PayPal partnership [techcrunch.com, Oct 28] is a payments/commerce deal. The Omnicom connection referenced in [marketing-interactive.com] describes Omnicom winning OpenAI as an advertising client (i.e., Omnicom handling OpenAI's marketing), not a formal OpenAI-Omnicom partnership in advertising. OpenAI's internal exploration of ads [moneycontrol.com, Nov 18; livemint.com, Nov 17] does not constitute a formal partnership announcement with a major advertising company.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with a clear timestamp was found within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found. OpenAI's advertising exploration is still in internal planning phases as of the window end.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches confirmed: (1) OpenAI is exploring ads but has not announced a formal advertising company partnership; (2) CEO Fidji Simo (formerly Meta) is discussing ad strategy but no deals announced; (3) News18 (Oct 29) explicitly noted 'OpenAI has not yet implemented ads...rollout unlikely within the next 6 to 12 months'; (4) The Omnicom win is Omnicom getting OpenAI as a creative client, not OpenAI partnering with Omnicom in advertising. No contradictory evidence found that would suggest a formal major advertising partnership occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The window closed (2025-11-23) without OpenAI announcing a formal partnership with a major advertising company. OpenAI's advertising plans remain exploratory/internal, and the only marketing agency partnership found (SearchKings) does not qualify as a 'major advertising company.' Resolution: No.

question: Will Atlas have an iOS app live by December 31?
description:

The application must be officially released by OpenAI or through official Atlas communication channels.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI announce a beta release of the Atlas iOS app before November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: OpenAI has recently launched its AI-powered web browser, Atlas, on macOS, with plans to release it on Windows, iOS, and Android soon. As of October 2025, ChatGPT has over 800 million weekly active users. OpenAI aims to increase internet traffic and digital advertising revenue with the release of Atlas. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if OpenAI officially announces a beta release of the Atlas iOS app between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive), as reported by reputable sources such as The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/) or TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/). The announcement must be made through official OpenAI channels or credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: A beta release of the Atlas iOS app would indicate that OpenAI is making progress towards releasing a native iOS application, which is a key factor in determining whether Atlas will have an iOS app live by December 31. This subquestion provides an early indicator of OpenAI's progress towards achieving this goal.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: OpenAI officially announces a beta release of an iOS app called 'Atlas' between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-15. Observable evidence: official OpenAI announcement or credible reporting (The Verge, TechCrunch, etc.) about 'Atlas iOS app' beta. Key entities: OpenAI, Atlas iOS app, beta release. The platform must be iOS specifically, not macOS.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI Atlas iOS app beta release' (Oct 23 - Nov 15, 2025) - to find direct iOS beta announcements; 2) 'OpenAI Atlas app announcement 2025' (Oct 1 - Nov 15, 2025) - broader search for any Atlas app announcement; 3) 'OpenAI Atlas iOS app beta November 2025' - narrowed iOS search; 4) 'ChatGPT Atlas iPhone iPad iOS release date' - finding any iOS launch; 5) 'OpenAI Atlas mobile iOS Android release launch' (Nov 1-15, 2025) - late-window search; 6) 'ChatGPT Atlas Windows iOS Android launch date announced' - looking for platform expansion news.
evidence.step3_event_detection: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas as a macOS-only web browser on October 21-23, 2025. Across 30+ articles reviewed, iOS (and Windows/Android) support is consistently described as 'planned for future release,' 'coming soon,' or 'forthcoming' with no timeline. GreekReporter (Oct 23) explicitly states: 'OpenAI has not yet announced release dates for Windows, iOS, or Android versions of Atlas.' Mashable (Oct 23): 'OpenAI has not announced a release timeline for Windows, iOS, or Android versions.' No article within or outside the resolution window reports any iOS beta or launch for Atlas.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of an 'Atlas iOS app beta release' by OpenAI within the Oct 23 – Nov 15 window. The macOS launch does not qualify (wrong platform). All sources report iOS as 'planned' with no announced timeline. The resolution criteria explicitly require a beta iOS app release — this condition was not met. Sources consulted include [PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/2950777/openai-launches-its-own-free-atlas-browser-with-chatgpt-built-in.html), [GreekReporter](https://greekreporter.com/2025/10/23/openai-web-browser-atlas-rival-google-chrome/), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/openai-new-web-browser-called-atlas/), [Mashable](https://me.mashable.com/tech/62810/chatgpt-atlas-how-to-install-openai-browser-installation-features-other-details), and many others.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for an Atlas iOS beta release because no such event occurred within the resolution window. The macOS launch occurred on October 21-23, 2025, but that is not an iOS app.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any late-November iOS Atlas articles — none found. The Nov 13-14 articles (KnowTechie GPT-5.1, iPhone in Canada group chats) still describe Atlas as a macOS browser only. Perplexity's Comet launched on Android in early November (Nov 10) with no mention of an Atlas iOS launch. No contradictory evidence found — all sources consistently indicate iOS support was not yet released by November 15, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution window closed on November 15, 2025 with no Atlas iOS app beta having been announced or released. All available evidence consistently shows that Atlas was macOS-only throughout the entire window, with iOS/Windows/Android described as 'coming soon' without a timeline. The condition for Yes resolution was never met. Resolution: No, with resolution_datetime set to the end of the window.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an official agreement on nuclear arms control or strategic nuclear weapons limitation is reached between the United States and the Russian Federation between August 14, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Russia engage in official nuclear arms control talks between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
The New START treaty, signed in 2010, limits each side to no more than 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 missiles or bombers. The treaty is set to expire on February 5, 2026. Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a one-year extension of the treaty, provided the United States agrees to do the same. The United States has yet to respond to the proposal. According to Daryl G. Kimball, Executive Director of the Arms Control Association, maintaining limits on the world's two largest nuclear arsenals will reduce tensions, prevent a costly arms race, and create diplomatic leverage to address China's nuclear buildup. [1](https://www.firstpost.com/world/uk-french-arsenals-must-be-part-of-any-us-russia-arms-control-deal-says-kremlin-13221541.html) [2](https://www.thenation.com/article/world/putin-new-start-treaty-nuclear-arms-control/). Firstpost: https://www.firstpost.com/
The Nation: https://www.thenation.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) confirm that nuclear arms control talks have begun between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. The primary resolution source will be official statements from the U.S. government and/or the Russian Federation, as reported by reputable news sources such as The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/) or BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it indicates whether the United States and Russia are making progress towards negotiating a new nuclear arms control agreement. If talks begin, it increases the likelihood of a successful agreement, which would in turn increase the likelihood of a positive resolution to the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Official US-Russia nuclear arms control talks must have formally begun between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, confirmed by official statements from US government (White House, State Department) and/or Russian Federation (Kremlin, MFA), as reported by reputable news sources. Observable evidence: Announcement of scheduled or ongoing bilateral nuclear arms control negotiations, not merely proposals, offers, or 'consideration.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Russia nuclear arms control talks 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find any news about talks starting; 2) 'United States Russia nuclear negotiations November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find specific negotiation events; 3) 'US Russia formal nuclear arms control talks begun started November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find evidence of talks actually commencing; 4) 'State Department Russia nuclear talks meeting November 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 30) — to find US-side confirmation of formal talks.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Russia proposed nuclear talks with US on Nov 11, 2025 (Lavrov offer); (B) US 'considering' Putin's New START proposal, communicated via diplomatic channels (Lavrov, Nov 9); (C) Trump said US, Russia, China are 'working on a denuclearization plan' (Nov 5), but Kremlin's Peskov denied any expert-level talks underway; (D) Russia signaling openness to US talks on nuclear stability (Putin, Nov 27); (E) Russia preparing to potentially resume dialogue at Conference on Disarmament in January 2026 (Gatilov, Nov 20). ALL rejected for Yes resolution because none represent actual formal talks having begun.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CNN (Nov 16) explicitly states: 'no formal talks have begun' despite Putin's proposal and Trump's positive initial response. [CNN](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty). TASS (Nov 5) reports Kremlin's Peskov 'confirmed on October 30, 2025, that Moscow and Washington are not currently engaged in expert-level talks on nuclear disarmament.' [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2039799). TASS (Nov 13): US 'has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals regarding New START.' [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2043379). TASS (Nov 20): Russia 'prepared to resume nuclear arms reduction dialogue...potentially at the Conference on Disarmament in January 2026' — future tense, not yet started. [TASS](https://tass.com/pressreview/2046027). TASS (Nov 26): Ryabkov states Russia 'remains unconvinced that the United States is ready to respect its core interests' and emphasizes conditions for resuming strategic dialogue — not yet happening. [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2049291). Devdiscourse (Nov 27): Putin 'announced Russia's willingness to engage in discussions' — willingness, not commencement. No source confirms talks actually began.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of formal talks beginning can be extracted, because no such event occurred. The absence is well-documented throughout the period.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (formal talks beginning) was found to check for first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, authoritative sources (CNN, TASS, Moscow Times, Anadolu Agency) consistently confirm no formal nuclear arms control talks between the US and Russia began during the window. The narrative is entirely about proposals, offers, and consideration — not actual talks. There is no contradictory evidence suggesting talks did begin.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is clear and unanimous: throughout October 31 – November 30, 2025, the US and Russia did not engage in official nuclear arms control talks. Russia made proposals (New START extension, offer to discuss nuclear testing allegations) and signaled readiness, but the US did not formally respond, and no talks were launched. CNN explicitly noted 'no formal talks have begun' as of November 16, 2025. Russia's envoy reported no reaction from the US to proposals as of November 13, and Ryabkov on November 26 described Russia as still needing to be convinced the US is ready to engage. The window closed on November 30 with no qualifying event. Resolution: No.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

(4) Reported by at least two reputable sources — Al Jazeera reported it at [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/18/whats-on-the-agenda-as-saudi-arabias-mbs-meets-trump-in-the-us), AFP reported it at [AFP](http://doc.afp.com/84EQ663), Al Arabiya reported at [Al Arabiya](https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2025/11/18/mbs-says-normalization-with-israel-hinges-on-clear-path-to-palestinian-state), Times of Israel reported it at [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/mbs-tells-trump-he-wants-to-join-abraham-accords-but-path-to-palestinian-state-crucial/), and Anadolu Agency at [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/saudi-crown-prince-says-he-wants-his-country-to-be-part-of-the-abraham-accords/3747375). (5) Within the window — November 18, 2025 is within Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025. The conditional nature of MBS's openness (requiring Palestinian statehood progress) does not negate that he expressed openness; expressing openness with conditions still constitutes expressing openness.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 18, 2025 — multiple sources provide this exact date for MBS's public statement at the White House Oval Office. The AFP article is explicitly dated 2025-11-18. Al Jazeera's article is explicitly dated 2025-11-18.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Within the resolution window (Oct 31–Nov 30, 2025), the November 18, 2025 statement is the first major public statement. Earlier articles (Nov 1–17) discuss Saudi Arabia's conditions and expectations ahead of the visit but are analyses/reports of Saudi position rather than direct public statements from senior officials expressing openness within the window. The first explicit public statement from MBS expressing openness occurred on November 18, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Some articles frame MBS as 'rejecting' normalization based on behind-closed-doors reports, but his public statements clearly expressed openness: 'We want peace for the Israelis. We want peace for the Palestinians... we want to be part of the Abraham Accords.' A U.S. official confirmed MBS 'never said no' to normalization. The resolution criteria require 'expressing openness to normalizing relations with Israel,' not committing to immediate normalization. MBS's public statement expressing that Saudi Arabia wants to join the Abraham Accords and will work toward normalization 'as soon as possible' clearly satisfies the 'expressing openness' threshold. Multiple reputable sources including Al Jazeera (specifically named in resolution criteria) reported this statement.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves Yes. On November 18, 2025 (within the Oct 31–Nov 30 window), Saudi Crown Prince MBS — the most senior Saudi official — publicly stated at the White House that Saudi Arabia wants to be part of the Abraham Accords and aims to normalize relations with Israel 'as soon as possible.' This was reported by Al Jazeera and numerous other reputable sources, easily satisfying the 'at least two reputable news sources' threshold. The statement constitutes 'expressing openness to normalizing relations with Israel' as required by the resolution criteria.

subquestions.question: Will the French 10-year bond yield increase by at least 10 basis points between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13?
subquestions.background_information: The French 10-year bond yield is a key indicator of the country's creditworthiness and economic health. As of September 12, 2025, the 10-year yield was at 3.47%, close to Italy's level, indicating market expectations of a downgrade <https://www.afp.com/en/news/3424/fitch-downgrades-frances-credit-rating-new-debt-blow>. A increase in the yield would suggest that investors are becoming more risk-averse and demanding higher returns for holding French debt, which could be a sign of a potential credit rating downgrade. According to Investing.com, France's sovereign debt rating is currently under review by Moody's, Fitch, and S&P Global <https://www.investing.com/news/economy/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3053464>.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the French 10-year bond yield increases by at least 10 basis points between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13, as reported by reputable financial news sources such as Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/> or Reuters <https://www.reuters.com/>. The yield values will be compared to the values reported on 2025-09-13. If the yield increase is 10 basis points or more, the question resolves Yes; otherwise, it resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The French 10-year bond yield is a key indicator of the country's creditworthiness and economic health. An increase in the yield could be a sign of a potential credit rating downgrade, which is the ultimate question. By monitoring the yield, we can gain insight into the market's expectations of France's creditworthiness and the potential for a downgrade.
Sources: AFP: Fitch downgrades France's credit rating in new debt blow
Investing.com: France faces sovereign rating test amid political chaos

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: French 10-year bond yield must increase by AT LEAST 10 basis points from its value on 2025-09-13 to any point between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (or at 2025-10-13). Observable evidence: yield values reported on September 13, 2025 and October 13, 2025 by reputable financial news sources. Key entities: French 10-year OAT bond. Threshold: ≥10 bps increase. Timing: start date 2025-09-13, end date 2025-10-13.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'French 10-year bond yield OAT September 2025' (Sep 10-20) to find Sep 13 yield; 2) 'French 10-year bond yield OAT October 2025' (Oct 10-14) to find Oct 13 yield; 3) 'France OAT 10-year yield September 13 2025 basis points' to confirm Sep 13 value; 4) 'French 10-year government bond OAT yield October 13 2025' to confirm Oct 13 value; 5) 'France OAT 10-year yield close September 13' for closing value; 6) 'French bond yield September 2025 highest level week October change basis points' for broader context.
evidence.step3_event_detection: September 13, 2025 yield: The Fitch downgrade was announced on Friday September 13, 2025. Multiple sources report the yield 'rose to 3.47%' on September 13 (Jakarta Post, AFP, Yahoo Finance). The September 12 article (InstaForex) shows the yield at 3.5% (anticipating the downgrade). On September 15 (Monday), CNBC reports the yield at 3.5132%, up 7 bps from ~3.44% (implying pre-downgrade close was ~3.44%). Cryptopolitan confirms '7 basis points higher to 3.5132%' from Friday's close. The Tradeweb Markets report confirms the September end yield was 3.47%. October 13, 2025 yield: InstaForex reports 3.46% ('lowest level in a month'); Economic Times reports 3.484%. Armstrong Economics market talk data shows 'France...all saw modest declines in yield' on Oct 13.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: September 13, 2025 yield: approximately 3.44-3.47% (Friday close; if Sep 13 was the last trading day before Monday's Fitch reaction, the yield was likely ~3.44% per the 7-bp rise to 3.5132% on Sep 15; or ~3.47% if reported as same-day closing). October 13, 2025 yield: approximately 3.46-3.484%. The change from Sep 13 to Oct 13 is: if Sep 13 = ~3.44%, change = +0.02 to +0.04 pp = +2 to +4 bps (No); if Sep 13 = ~3.47%, change = -0.01 to +0.01 pp = -1 to +1 bps (No). In neither scenario does the yield increase reach 10 basis points. [InstaForex Oct 13](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/2773654) [Economic Times Oct 13](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/bonds/french-yields-edge-up-focus-on-paris-politics-us-tariffs/articleshow/124521959.cms)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 13, 2025: yield at ~3.44-3.47% (Friday close/Saturday announcement). October 13, 2025: yield at 3.46-3.484% (Monday intraday, per Economic Times and InstaForex articles published on October 13, 2025). These are reliable timestamps from the published dates.
evidence.step7_verification: The Tradeweb Markets September 2025 report (published Oct 3) confirms French 10-year OAT yield 'fell to 3.47% by month-end' (September end), down 3 bps — consistent with a September 13 yield around 3.5%. Peak during the period: 3.60% on Sep 26 (InstaForex), and 3.587% on Oct 6 (InstaForex). However, these intermediate highs do not define the Oct 13 closing value. The Oct 13 yield was clearly around 3.46-3.484%, lower than the Sep 13 yield of ~3.47-3.50%. French bond yields DECREASED over the period, not increased. The question asks specifically about the increase between Sep 13 and Oct 13. No 10 bps increase is supported.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The French 10-year bond yield on September 13, 2025 was approximately 3.44-3.47%. By October 13, 2025, the yield was approximately 3.46-3.484%. This represents at most a ~1-4 bps change, far below the 10 bps threshold required for Yes resolution. The yield actually declined over this period. Resolution: No.

question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un exchange public messages or statements about a potential meeting between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information: There have been recent discussions about a potential meeting between Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
