subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un exchange public messages or statements about a potential meeting, as reported by reputable news sources such as The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), or official government websites. The resolution source will check for statements or messages on official social media accounts, including Twitter (https://twitter.com/) and Truth Social, as well as official press releases and statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the North Korean government.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides an indicator of the likelihood of a meeting between Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. If they exchange public messages or statements about a potential meeting, it could suggest that a meeting is more likely to occur, which would be a positive indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires BOTH Trump AND Kim Jong Un to exchange public messages or statements ABOUT a potential meeting between them, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. This is an 'exchange,' meaning both sides must have made public statements directed at or about each other regarding a potential meeting. The resolution criteria require this to be reported by reputable news sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump Kim Jong Un meeting statement October 2025' — to find statements from either leader; 2) 'North Korea Kim Jong Un Trump message public exchange 2025' — to find any North Korean public statements; 3) 'Kim Jong Un response Trump meeting invitation October 2025' — to find Kim's response to Trump; 4) 'North Korea KCNA statement Trump Kim summit October 2025' — to find KCNA official communications; 5) 'North Korea silent Trump APEC no response Kim' — to verify whether North Korea responded.
evidence.step3_event_detection: TRUMP STATEMENTS (within window): Numerous public statements by Trump throughout October 2025 about wanting to meet Kim: Oct 1 White House official statement on 'no preconditions'; Oct 24-25 Trump says 'open to it 100%' and asks media to 'put out the word'; Oct 27 Trump says 'I'd love to meet with him'; Oct 29 Trump says 'timing didn't work out.' KIM JONG UN STATEMENTS (within window): The key question is whether Kim made any public statements within the Oct 1-31 window ABOUT a potential meeting with Trump. The evidence shows: (a) Kim's Sep 21 statement (BEFORE the window) about willingness to meet if US drops denuclearization demand; (b) North Korea's state media KCNA remained SILENT on Trump's overtures throughout October; (c) North Korea responded to Trump's offers with a cruise missile test on Oct 28, but KCNA did not mention Trump's meeting invitations; (d) Kim publicly inspected a hospital on Oct 30 with no mention of Trump; (e) North Korea's FM Choe Son-hui made statements in Minsk (Oct 29) criticizing US but not addressing the meeting offer. Multiple reputable sources (Yonhap, CNN, Korea Times, AP, Korea Herald, The Star) confirm North Korea remained SILENT on Trump's meeting offers throughout the October window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: For the question to resolve YES, there must be an EXCHANGE — both Trump AND Kim making public statements about a potential meeting. Trump clearly made multiple such statements within the window. However, multiple reputable sources confirm Kim Jong Un made NO public statement within the October 1-31 window about a potential meeting with Trump: [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20251029009751315) states Trump said 'timing didn't work out' and 'North Korea did not respond publicly to the offer'; [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffairs/northkorea/20251028/trump-renews-call-for-kim-meeting-but-north-korea-remains-silent) confirms 'North Korea remains silent'; [CNN](https://us.cnn.com/2025/10/30/asia/us-north-korea-trump-kim-analysis-intl-hnk) confirms 'North Korea's state media remained silent, with no mention of his visit or overtures'; [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/north-korea-missiles-611a288d8f6cb02f5d43bb5db70204f8) confirms 'North Korea has not responded to Trump's outreach'; [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/10/28/trump-would-039love039-to-meet-kim-jong-un-again-but-no-word-from-north-korea) confirms 'no word from North Korea.' Kim's earlier statement from September 21, 2025 (before the window) was the last known public statement from Kim about a potential meeting. Kim's speech on Oct 10 at the WPK anniversary did not address Trump or a meeting. There was NO exchange within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Trump's first qualifying statement within window: October 1, 2025 (White House official statement about 'no preconditions'). Kim Jong Un's qualifying statement within window: NONE FOUND. The September 21 statement is outside the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Trump's side: First statement in window is October 1. Kim's side: No qualifying statement found within the October 1-31 window. Without a statement from Kim within the window, there is no 'exchange' and the question cannot resolve Yes.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some articles reference Kim's September 21 statement as context, but this is before the window. No article reports Kim making any public statement within October 2025 about a potential meeting with Trump. North Korea's silence is confirmed by CNN, AP, Yonhap, Korea Times, Korea Herald, and multiple other reputable sources. North Korea's response during the window was a cruise missile test (Oct 28) — an action, not a public statement about a meeting. North Korea's FM Choe Son-hui criticized the US in Minsk (Oct 29) but did not address the meeting offer. The resolution criteria require an 'exchange' of public messages or statements — one-sided outreach from Trump does not qualify. The criteria is not met.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question requires BOTH leaders to exchange public messages/statements about a potential meeting. While Trump made numerous public statements in October 2025 expressing desire to meet Kim, Kim Jong Un made NO public statement within the October 1-31 window about a potential meeting with Trump. North Korea's state media (KCNA) remained completely silent on Trump's overtures. The one-sided nature of the exchange means the resolution criteria for 'exchange' is not satisfied. The window closed (October 31) without Kim making any public statement about a meeting. Resolution: NO.

question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla release a software update for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature with a 10x increase in parameters before October 1, 2025?

This update is expected to enable the system to consider more factors, look into the future, and have better intuition about upcoming events. However, Tesla's previous promises of improved FSD performance have not been met, with the system showing no meaningful improvement and even deteriorating in some cases <https://electrek.co/2025/08/elon-musk-teases-new-tesla-full-self-driving-supervised/>. On the other hand, if the update is not released, it could indicate that Tesla is facing challenges in developing its FSD feature, which could impact its ability to launch unsupervised FSD by the ultimate question's deadline.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Tesla must release a FSD software update with a 10x increase in parameters between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). (2) September 25, 2025 – Musk announced 'early wide' release of FSD V14 'next week.' [TESLARATI (Oct 7)](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-fsd-supervised-v14-robotaxi-style-dropoffs-release-notes/) confirms V14.1 with '10x higher parameter count' rolled out October 7. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The actual public release of FSD V14/V14.1 with 10x parameters occurred on October 6–7, 2025, which is outside the resolution window. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Tesla's FSD V14 update with 10x parameters was repeatedly announced and teased during September 2025 but was not publicly released until October 6–7, 2025, after the October 1, 2025 resolution deadline. question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US and Ukraine jointly announce a draft security guarantee agreement by November 30, 2025?

evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly shows that: (a) the US House of Representatives was in recess throughout virtually all of October 2025 due to the government shutdown, (b) the crypto tax hearing in October 2025 was held by the Senate Finance Committee, not the House, (c) the last House hearing on crypto taxation occurred in July 2025, and (d) no news reports or official sources mention any House hearing on cryptocurrency tax exemption in October 2025. Resolution is No. The window closed on October 31, 2025 with no qualifying event.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass at least 5 of the remaining 9 fiscal 2026 appropriations bills by January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. government is facing a potential shutdown on January 30, 2026, if Congress fails to pass spending bills by then. As of January 9, 2026, Congress has not passed any spending bills since the 43-day government shutdown ended on November 12, 2025, leaving nine of the 12 annual appropriations bills operating on stopgap funding that expires on January 30, 2026. According to an article by the Washington Times, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) and Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer (D-NY) both expressed confidence that Congress will avoid another shutdown (https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-in-catch-up-mode/). House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole (OK) announced a deal with Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins (ME) on topline funding levels for the remaining nine bills, with the total spending projected to be below the previous fiscal year’s $1.6 trillion (https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-in-catch-up-mode/). Sources: 
Washington Times: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-in-catch-up-mode/
One America News Network: https://www.oann.com/congress-debuts-174b-spending-package-as-jan-30-govt-shutdown-deadline-looms/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes at least 5 of the remaining 9 fiscal 2026 appropriations bills between January 9, 2026, and January 20, 2026, as reported by the House Appropriations Committee (https://appropriations.house.gov/) or the Congressional Budget Office (https://www.cbo.gov/).
subquestions.rationale: Passing at least 5 of the remaining 9 fiscal 2026 appropriations bills by January 20, 2026, would indicate progress towards avoiding a government shutdown and potentially reduce the likelihood of a shutdown, which is relevant to the ultimate question of whether there will be no US government shutdown by January 31 and whether the Republican Party will win the House in 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The U.S. House of Representatives must pass AT LEAST 5 of the remaining 9 fiscal 2026 appropriations bills between Jan 9–20, 2026. The 9 remaining bills (before the window) were: Commerce-Justice-Science, Energy-Water, Interior-Environment, Financial Services, State/National Security, Defense, Labor-HHS-Education, Transportation-HUD, and Homeland Security. Observable evidence: explicit news reports of House floor votes on these bills within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'House of Representatives fiscal 2026 appropriations bills passed January 2026' (Jan 9–20) — to identify bills passed in the window. 2) 'House appropriations bills vote January 2026 FY2026' (Jan 1–20) — to verify timing and count. 3) 'House passes defense labor transportation appropriations January 19 20 2026' — to check if final 4 bills were passed before Jan 20. 4) 'FY2026 House appropriations total bills passed count January 2026' — to verify cumulative totals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Jan 9: House passed 3-bill minibus (Commerce-Justice-Science, Energy-Water, Interior-Environment) 397-28. (B) Jan 14/15: House passed 2-bill minibus (Financial Services + State/National Security) 341-79. (C) Jan 20: Final 4-bill package (Defense, Labor-HHS-Ed, Transportation-HUD, DHS) was RELEASED/UNVEILED — articles explicitly state the House 'aims to complete work this week' and 'is expected to vote,' meaning the vote had NOT occurred on Jan 20. Event C is rejected as no vote occurred within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Bills passed by the House within window: (A) Jan 9 — 3 bills: [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/policy/house-approves-three-more-2026-funding-bills), [E&E News](https://www.eenews.net/articles/house-sends-energy-environment-spending-bills-to-the-senate/); (B) Jan 14 — 2 bills: [Washington Times](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/14/house-passes-spending-bill-foreign-aid-financial-services/), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5689765-house-passes-two-bill-package-to-fund-treasury-state-departments/), [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/4419139/house-passes-two-funding-bills-homeland-security-remains-flux/). Total = 5 bills passed within window. The Washington Times article dated Jan 14 explicitly states 'eight of the 12 annual appropriations bills had been passed by the House' as of Jan 14; 3 were passed before the window (Agriculture, Military Construction/VA, Legislative Branch from November 2025), so 5 were passed within the window. This exactly meets the threshold of 'at least 5.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: Jan 9, 2026 — House passed 3 bills (397-28 vote). Second qualifying event: Jan 14, 2026 — House passed 2 more bills (341-79 vote). Combined total = 5 bills, reaching the threshold on January 14, 2026. Multiple sources confirm the Jan 14 vote date explicitly.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The 5th bill passed on January 14, 2026, which is within the window (Jan 9–20, 2026). No earlier combination of 5 bills within the window could have occurred before Jan 14, since only 3 were passed on Jan 9. The threshold of 5 was reached on Jan 14, 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: One RedState article mentions 'three of twelve required appropriations bills had passed the House' as of the article's publication date (Jan 14), but this appears to refer to bills signed into law (not House-passed). The Washington Times article from Jan 14 clarifies '8 of 12 had been passed by the House,' which is consistent: 3 from November + 3 on Jan 9 + 2 on Jan 14 = 8. The question counts remaining 9 starting bills, with 5 passed in the window — exactly meeting the threshold. Jan 20 articles confirm the final 4 bills were only RELEASED on Jan 20 (not voted on), so they do not count within the window. No contradictory evidence found that would change the conclusion.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The House passed exactly 5 of the remaining 9 FY2026 appropriations bills within the Jan 9–20, 2026 window: 3 bills on January 9 and 2 more on January 14. The threshold of 'at least 5' was reached on January 14, 2026. The condition is satisfied. Resolution: Yes.

question: Negative GDP growth in Q4 2025?
description:
"This market will resolve to 'Yes' if the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP 'Advance Estimate' for Q4 2025, scheduled for release by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on January 29, 2026, reports a growth rate below 0. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'.

The GDP release will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Advance Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered."

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) report a decline in the annualized growth rate of real GDP for Q3 2025, compared to Q2 2025, in its 'Advance Estimate' release between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) has reported a real GDP growth rate of 3.3% for Q2 2025, with revisions driven by upward changes to investment and consumer spending, and a downward revision to government spending. The Q2 growth rate was also influenced by a decline in imports and an acceleration in consumer spending. The current state of the U.S. economy, including the impact of tariffs and AI investment, will likely influence the Q3 growth rate. According to the BEA, the 'Advance Estimate' for Q3 2025 is scheduled for release on October 29, 2025, but may be revised. For more information, see the BEA's website: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. The BEA's data on GDP growth rates can be found at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product#table_1.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the BEA reports a decline in the annualized growth rate of real GDP for Q3 2025, compared to Q2 2025, in its 'Advance Estimate' release between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29. The resolution will be based on the data available at the BEA's website: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. The 'Advance Estimate' for Q3 2025 will be used for resolution, and any subsequent revisions will not be considered. The start date for this question is 2025-10-30, and the end date is 2025-11-29.
subquestions.rationale: The U.S. GDP growth rate is a key indicator of the overall health of the economy. A decline in the growth rate for Q3 2025, compared to Q2 2025, could indicate a slowdown in economic activity, which may be relevant to the ultimate question of negative GDP growth in Q4 2025. The BEA's 'Advance Estimate' release is a reliable source of data on GDP growth rates, and the comparison between Q2 and Q3 growth rates can provide insight into the trajectory of the economy.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The BEA must publish its 'Advance Estimate' of Q3 2025 real GDP growth between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29, AND that Q3 figure must be lower than the Q2 2025 annualized growth rate. Observable evidence: BEA press release or website update within the window showing a specific Q3 2025 annualized GDP growth rate lower than Q2's 3.8% annualized rate. Key entities: BEA; key threshold: Q3 rate < Q2 rate (3.8%); timing: release between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BEA Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP Q3 2025 advance estimate' (to find whether a release occurred); Query 2: 'US real GDP growth rate Q3 2025 annualized advance estimate' (to find the actual reported figure); Query 3: 'BEA GDP advance estimate cancelled government shutdown October 2025' (to find evidence of cancellation); Query 4: 'Q3 2025 GDP December 23 release date BEA advance estimate rescheduled' (to confirm rescheduling outside window).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) BEA cancellation of Q3 2025 Advance GDP Estimate due to 43-day federal government shutdown - confirmed by multiple sources around Nov 24-25, 2025. (2) Q3 GDP estimate rescheduled to December 23, 2025. (3) Atlanta Fed GDPNow model projecting ~3.9-4.2% Q3 growth, Bank of America tracking at 2.8% Q3 growth - these are private forecasts NOT the official BEA Advance Estimate. No BEA Advance Estimate was published within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require the BEA to publish its 'Advance Estimate' within the window. Multiple sources confirm this did not happen: [BEA cancellation via Asianet News](https://newsable.asianetnews.com/markets/bea-cancels-q3-2025-gdp-advance-estimate-due-to-43-day-federal-shutdown-articleshow-209g9cf), [Market Screener Nov 24](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/u-s-to-skip-publication-of-initial-3q-gdp-estimate-ce7d5eddd989f72c), [Benzinga Nov 25 - rescheduled to Dec 23](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/economic-data/25/11/49052041/us-commerce-department-pushes-q3-gdp-estimate-to-just-before-christmas-stirring-political-jabs), [Market Screener Nov 25 - Dec 23 date confirmed](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/delayed-3q-gdp-estimate-now-scheduled-for-dec-23-ce7d5eddd88df225). The condition for Yes is definitively not met as the Advance Estimate was never released within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BEA cancellation was formally confirmed on November 24, 2025 (multiple sources: AFP, Market Screener, Asianet News). The reschedule to December 23 was announced November 25, 2025. The original scheduled date of October 30 passed without release. The resolution window closes November 29, 2025, and no release occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is no earlier qualifying occurrence because the BEA never released the Advance Estimate within the window at all. The BEA itself confirmed cancellation on November 24, 2025, and a new date of December 23, 2025 was announced on November 25, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Verified through multiple independent sources (AFP, Market Screener, Benzinga, Newsweek, Yahoo Finance, CalculatedRisk) that the BEA Advance Estimate for Q3 2025 was not released within the window. The Q2 2025 annualized growth rate was 3.8%. Private forecasts (Atlanta Fed GDPNow: ~3.9-4.2%, Bank of America: 2.8%) exist but do not constitute the official BEA Advance Estimate. No contradictory evidence found suggesting the Advance Estimate was released within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BEA canceled/skipped the Advance Estimate for Q3 2025 GDP due to the 43-day federal government shutdown. The report was originally scheduled for October 30, 2025, but was never released within the window (2025-10-30 to 2025-11-29). It was rescheduled to December 23, 2025. Since the required event (BEA publishing the Advance Estimate within the window) definitively did not occur, the question resolves No. The condition became definitively impossible by November 24-25, 2025 when the BEA formally confirmed cancellation and rescheduled to December 23.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly supports resolution as Yes. subquestions.question: Will the FDIC's Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) reserve ratio increase by at least 0.5% between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information: The FDIC's Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) is a critical component of the US banking system, providing insurance coverage for depositors in the event of a bank failure. As of November 2025, the DIF's reserve ratio was nearing its legal target ratio, driven by $3.3 billion in assessment revenue and an additional $2.1 billion from interest on investment securities, negative provisions for insurance losses, and unrealized gains on securities. The FDIC has been rebuilding the fund since 2020, when the reserve ratio fell below the legal minimum due to pandemic-driven deposit surges. According to the FDIC, the DIF is expected to reach its required reserve ratio by the end of 2025. [1](https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/), [2](https://www.pymnts.com/news/banking/2025/fdic-deposit-insurance-fund-nears-legal-target-ratio/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the FDIC's Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) reserve ratio increases by at least 0.5% between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12, as reported by the FDIC on its website: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/. The resolution will be based on the official data published by the FDIC.
subquestions.rationale: The FDIC's Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) reserve ratio is a key indicator of the stability of the US banking system. An increase in the reserve ratio would suggest that the FDIC is making progress in rebuilding the fund and reducing the risk of bank failures, which is relevant to the ultimate question of whether a US bank will fail by March 31, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: FDIC DIF reserve ratio must increase by at least 0.5 percentage points (50 basis points) between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12. Observable evidence: Official FDIC data showing DIF reserve ratio values at start and end of period. Key entities: FDIC, Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF). Threshold: +0.5% (50 bp) increase. Timing: 30-day window from Dec 13, 2025 to Jan 12, 2026.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'FDIC Deposit Insurance Fund DIF reserve ratio 2025 2026' - to find current values. 2. 'FDIC DIF reserve ratio increase bank failures 2025' - to find historical trend. 3. 'FDIC reserve ratio 1.28% 1.29% 2025 quarterly banking profile' - to find specific values. 4. 'FDIC quarterly banking profile Q4 2025 Deposit Insurance Fund balance' - for any Q4 update. 5. 'FDIC failed bank list reserve ratio December 2025 January 2026' - to check for updates in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key data found: Q3 2025 Quarterly Banking Profile (released November 24, 2025) shows DIF reserve ratio at 1.4% (up 4 basis points from Q2 2025's 1.36%). Q2 2025 was the first quarter to exceed the statutory minimum of 1.35%. No Q4 2025 data was published within the question window (Dec 13, 2025 - Jan 12, 2026). The FDIC's DIF reserve ratio is a quarterly metric, not updated monthly. The Quarterly Banking Profile for Q4 2025 (Oct-Dec 2025) would not be published until approximately late February 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found of ANY DIF reserve ratio update published between Dec 13, 2025 and Jan 12, 2026. The resolution criteria reference the failed bank list URL (https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/) which does NOT show the DIF reserve ratio - this URL shows failed bank data, not the reserve ratio. The DIF reserve ratio is reported in the Quarterly Banking Profile. Furthermore, a 0.5% (50 bp) increase in 30 days is approximately 12x the typical quarterly increase of ~4 bp. There is no mechanism by which the DIF reserve ratio could increase by 50 bp in a 30-day window: [FDIC Q3 2025 QBP](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2025/11/quarterly-banking-profile-banking-net-income-79-3-billion-in-q3-2025/), [PYMNTS DIF](https://www.pymnts.com/news/banking/2025/fdics-deposit-insurance-fund-reserve-ratio-exceeds-statutory-minimum-for-second-consecutive-quarter/).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no such event occurred. The FDIC DIF reserve ratio data is only published quarterly, approximately 8 weeks after quarter end. The Q3 2025 data was published November 24, 2025 (before the window). The Q4 2025 data would not be published until approximately late February 2026 (after the window). No intra-quarter DIF reserve ratio updates exist.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found. The DIF reserve ratio increased by only 4 basis points (0.04%) in Q3 2025, and this data was published before the window started. No new DIF reserve ratio data was published within the window. The question window is entirely within the gap between quarterly FDIC reports.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple contradictory points against Yes resolution: (1) The FDIC reports DIF reserve ratio quarterly, not within this window; (2) Historical rate of change is ~4-8 bp per quarter, far less than the required 50 bp; (3) The resolution criteria cite an incorrect URL (failed bank list) for this data; (4) No news articles from Dec 13, 2025 - Jan 12, 2026 mention any DIF reserve ratio update; (5) The FDIC's DRR remained at 2% (target, not current ratio) - this is a different metric. The question appears to conflate the current reserve ratio (~1.4%) with a rapid increase threshold that is structurally impossible in a 30-day window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively No. The FDIC DIF reserve ratio: (a) was at 1.4% as of Q3 2025 (published Nov 24, 2025, before window start); (b) only updates quarterly; (c) Q4 2025 data would not be published until ~late February 2026; (d) historically increases by ~4 basis points per quarter, making a 50 bp increase in 30 days impossible; (e) no evidence of any DIF reserve ratio data published within the Dec 13, 2025 - Jan 12, 2026 window. The condition became definitively impossible from the start of the window because no qualifying data update could or did occur within the window.

question: Trump x Putin Meeting in Hungary by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin meet in Hungary at any time by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A meeting is defined as any encounter where Trump and Putin are both present and interact with each other in person.

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors take place before November 17, 2025, as a precursor to the potential Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary?
subquestions.background_information: According to recent news articles, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin have agreed to meet in Budapest, Hungary, to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. A high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors is scheduled to take place before the Trump-Putin meeting, as reported by DNA India and TASS. This meeting is seen as a crucial step towards resolving the Ukraine conflict. As of now, the exact date of the meeting is not confirmed, but it is expected to take place soon. Sources: DNA India: https://www.dnaindia.com/ TASS: https://tass.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors takes place between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17, as reported by credible news sources such as Reuters or BBC News. The meeting must be confirmed by at least two reputable news outlets to be considered as having taken place.
subquestions.rationale: The high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors is a crucial precursor to the potential Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary. If this meeting takes place, it could indicate a positive development towards resolving the Ukraine conflict and increase the likelihood of a successful Trump-Putin meeting.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: A high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors must have taken place between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17, explicitly as a precursor to a potential Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary (Budapest), confirmed by at least two reputable news outlets. Key entities: U.S. advisors (Rubio, Witkoff), Russian advisors (Lavrov, Dmitriev). The meeting must be in-person or at least a confirmed high-level interaction.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US Russia advisors high-level meeting Trump Putin Hungary 2025' — to find general context; 2) 'Trump Putin meeting Hungary precursor advisor talks' — to find specific preparatory meetings; 3) 'Rubio Lavrov meeting took place October November 2025' — to find the Rubio-Lavrov meeting; 4) 'US Russia high level advisors meeting held confirmed 2025' — to find confirmed meetings; 5) 'Kirill Dmitriev Witkoff meeting October November 2025' — to find the Dmitriev-Witkoff meeting; 6) 'Rubio Lavrov face-to-face meeting in-person Budapest October 2025' — to check if an in-person Lavrov-Rubio meeting occurred; 7) 'US Russia envoy advisor meeting November 2025 Ukraine peace talks' — to find any November meetings.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Lavrov-Rubio phone call on October 20, 2025 — confirmed by multiple credible sources (Russian Foreign Ministry, State Department, Straits Times, Anadolu Agency, TASS, Asharq Al-Awsat) as 'constructive' and explicitly preparatory for the Trump-Putin Budapest summit. This is a high-level advisor interaction within the window. (B) Planned face-to-face Rubio-Lavrov meeting (originally Oct 23, then reportedly Oct 30 in Budapest) — REJECTED: Multiple sources confirm this was postponed indefinitely. The White House confirmed via CNN that the in-person meeting was postponed. No face-to-face Rubio-Lavrov meeting took place. (C) Dmitriev-Witkoff in-person meetings in Miami, October 25-27, 2025 — Confirmed by multiple sources (Axios/TASS, Straits Times, Yahoo News, TASS Oct 26 follow-up, Devdiscourse, Gateway Pundit, APA). Dmitriev is Putin's special envoy; Witkoff is Trump's special envoy. The meetings occurred over three days and were explicitly connected to U.S.-Russia diplomatic engagement amid preparations for a Trump-Putin summit.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Two distinct qualifying events occurred within the window: (1) The Lavrov-Rubio phone call on October 20, 2025, confirmed by [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/Russia-says-Lavrov-and-Rubio-held-constructive-pre-summit-call), [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/russia-ukraine-war/russia-us-hold-constructive-talks-ahead-of-putin-trump-summit-in-budapest/3722051), [TASS](https://tass.com/politics/2032573), [Asharq Al-Awsat](https://english.aawsat.com/node/5199435). Lavrov (Russian Foreign Minister) and Rubio (U.S. Secretary of State) are the highest-level diplomatic advisors. The call was explicitly described as 'preparatory work for the upcoming Trump-Putin summit' in Budapest. (2) Dmitriev-Witkoff in-person meetings October 25-27, 2025, confirmed by [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2034801), [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/Putin-envoy-Kirill-Dmitriev-confirms-he-is-in-the-US-for-a-long-planned-meeting), [Yahoo News](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/russian-special-envoy-us-says-061026870.html), [TASS follow-up](https://tass.com/politics/2035135), and [Devdiscourse](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3673099-high-stakes-dialogue-us-and-russian-envoys-convene). Both Dmitriev (Putin's special envoy) and Witkoff (Trump's special envoy) are high-level advisors. The resolution criteria specifies a 'high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors,' and both events qualify. The phone call between Lavrov and Rubio on October 20 constitutes an advisor-level high-level meeting. The in-person Dmitriev-Witkoff meetings on October 25-27 further confirm the pattern. The resolution criteria does not specify that the meeting must be in-person, only that it is 'high-level' and between 'advisors.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: Lavrov-Rubio phone call on October 20, 2025. Multiple sources explicitly state the date as October 20, 2025. TASS published at 2025-10-20, Straits Times published at 2025-10-20, Anadolu Agency published at 2025-10-20. Timestamp: 2025-10-20 (date only, exact time not specified in articles). evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying high-level meeting is the Lavrov-Rubio phone call on October 20, 2025. This is the earliest confirmed high-level U.S.-Russia advisor interaction within the window (October 18–November 17, 2025). No earlier qualifying event within the window has been found (the window starts October 18, and no meetings between October 18-19 are mentioned).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: Some articles report the planned face-to-face Rubio-Lavrov meeting was 'postponed indefinitely' or 'canceled.' However, this refers to the in-person face-to-face meeting, not the October 20 phone call which DID take place. The resolution criteria asks for 'a high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors' — it does not specify in-person. A phone call between the Secretary of State and Foreign Minister constitutes a high-level diplomatic meeting. Furthermore, the Dmitriev-Witkoff in-person meetings on October 25-27 are confirmed by multiple sources as having taken place. The Dmitriev-Witkoff meeting is explicitly an in-person meeting between presidential envoys from both sides, squarely qualifying as a 'high-level meeting between U.S. and Russian advisors.' Additionally, the November 13 article from TASS mentions that 'Russia-US dialogue is ongoing' and refers to these interactions. The resolution criteria requires confirmation by 'at least two reputable news outlets' — both the Lavrov-Rubio call and the Dmitriev-Witkoff meeting are confirmed by multiple reputable outlets.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Yes, the question resolves Yes. Within the window of October 18–November 17, 2025, at least two qualifying high-level meetings between U.S. and Russian advisors occurred as precursors to a potential Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary: (1) The Lavrov-Rubio phone call on October 20, 2025, explicitly described as preparatory for the Budapest Trump-Putin summit, confirmed by multiple reputable sources. (2) The Dmitriev-Witkoff in-person meetings in Miami on October 25-27, 2025, confirmed by multiple reputable sources. Both events qualify as 'high-level meeting[s] between U.S. and Russian advisors' as precursors to the potential Trump-Putin meeting in Hungary. The first qualifying event occurred on October 20, 2025.
